steps.message:
Dale's comment G-4 wants freeboard dimensioning, sizing calculations and apron details for the emergency spillway on C-9. Before I put the drainage lead on it I need to know whether the spillway as drawn holds up. Work it against the improvement plans and the QA/QC checklist in Design-Drafting, the master drainage study and the storm drain worksheets in Reports-Studies, and the Phase 2 comments and the flood control district acceptance letter in Correspondence/Agency. Tell me whether we can answer G-4 with what's on the sheet today and whether the revisions trigger an amendment to the accepted master study, what the spillway detail and the basin notes have to say on the revised C-9, and where the overflow ends up once it leaves the berm. Put it in a memo to Callaway for my signature, dated 10/31/2026.

Save it as /filesystem/Memo_to_Callaway_Spillway_2026-10-31.docx. Commit to one disposition on each question rather than giving me options. Put units on every value and name the record it comes from. Do not round intermediate values. Work to professional engineering standards.

1. INTRODUCTION AND PROJECT DESCRIPTION
1.1 Purpose
The purpose of this Master Drainage Study is to establish the hydrologic and hydraulic basis of design for storm
drainage improvements serving the Desert Sage Ranch subdivision, a 140-acre residential development to be
constructed in three phases in the Enterprise area of unincorporated Clark County, Nevada. This study is
submitted to the Clark County Regional Flood Control District (CCRFCD) for acceptance and, upon acceptance,
is intended to serve as the master planning document governing all subsequent improvement plan submittals for
the individual phases.
1.2 Project Location
Desert Sage Ranch occupies a portion of Section 27, Township 22 South, Range 60 East, M.D.M., in
unincorporated Clark County. The site is bounded generally by Rainbow Boulevard on the west and Windmill
Lane on the south, with the project address of record identified as Rainbow Boulevard and Windmill Lane, Las
Vegas, Nevada 89178. Assessor Parcel Number 177-27-201-001 encompasses the balance of the site not
already partitioned.
The site is located within the Enterprise Town Advisory Board area of unincorporated Clark County and is
governed by Clark County Code Title 30. Land use planning oversight is exercised by Clark County
Comprehensive Planning.
1.3 Site Description and Development
The 140-acre site is generally undeveloped desert terrain sloping gently from the northeast to the southwest at
an average grade of approximately 1.6 percent. Native ground cover consists of sparse creosote and bursage
on gravelly, well-drained soils overlying a caliche-influenced subsurface typical of the Enterprise sub-basin.
There are no defined natural watercourses across the site; historic runoff sheet-flows to the southwest.
Desert Sage Ranch will be developed as a single-family residential subdivision served by public streets. Phase
3 consists of 60 half-acre lots (100 ft × 220 ft, approximately 22,000 sf); Phases 1 and 2 consist of smaller
residential lots (approximately 6,050 sf, 55 ft × 110 ft) per the recorded Phase 1-2 Final Map. The full 140 acres
will be built out in three sequential phases:
• Phase 1 — 45.0 acres, northern portion of the site.
• Phase 2 — 55.0 acres, central portion of the site.
• Phase 3 — 40.0 acres, southern portion of the site, comprising 60 half-acre lots and associated street
frontage, HOA common-area park and streetscape improvements.
Each phase will be constructed under its own improvement plan set, prepared to be consistent with this Master
Drainage Study.


--- page 3 ---
1.4 Regulatory Framework
This study has been prepared in conformance with:
• Clark County Regional Flood Control District Hydrologic Criteria and Drainage Design Manual, edition
applicable at the time of preparation;
• Clark County Uniform Standard Drawings and applicable Public Works standards;
• Clark County Code Title 30 (development standards).
Hydrologic and hydraulic methods, precipitation input, loss rates and detention criteria are drawn from the
CCRFCD manual as it stood at the time of study preparation and acceptance. Subsequent phase-level design
shall comply with the master allocations set forth herein.
1.5 Study Deliverables
This document establishes:
• Design storm criteria and rainfall depths.
• Tributary-area delineation for the full 140 acres, broken down by development phase.
• Peak discharge estimates for the tributary sub-basins under fully developed conditions.
• A shared onsite detention approach with a fixed allocation of storage volume to each phase.
• Allowance for the full 140 acres at a shared outfall to the downstream regional facility, with a maximum
permitted discharge.
• A phasing exhibit identifying phase boundaries and detention basin locations.
2. EXISTING CONDITIONS AND OFFSITE TRIBUTARY
2.1 Topography and Soils
Existing topography across the 140-acre site is a gently sloping desert plain. Elevations range from
approximately 2,905 feet at the northeast corner to approximately 2,850 feet at the southwest outfall point,
yielding an average site slope of approximately 1.6 percent to the southwest.
Surface soils across the site are classified as SM to SP-SM (silty sands and poorly graded sands with silt), with
cemented caliche horizons at variable depth. Infiltration rates in the caliche zone are low, and no percolation
credit is taken in the hydrologic analysis. The full computed runoff volume is treated as surface flow for the
purposes of this study.
2.2 Existing Drainage Pattern
Under existing conditions, stormwater sheet-flows overland from north-northeast to south-southwest across the
site. There are no defined channels within the property boundaries. At the southwest corner of the site, runoff


--- page 4 ---
historically discharges toward the downstream regional drainage facility maintained by CCRFCD.
2.3 Offsite Tributary from the North
The site accepts a modest offsite drainage flow entering along the northern boundary of what will become Phase
1. The offsite tributary area upstream of the north boundary consists of approximately 38 acres of low-density
residential and open desert land. Under fully developed offsite conditions consistent with the surrounding land
use plan, the offsite peak inflow at the northern site boundary has been estimated as summarized in Section 3
and Appendix C.
The offsite tributary flow enters the site as sheet flow along the northern boundary and, at build-out, will be
conveyed through the Phase 1 street network to the shared onsite detention basin(s). No offsite bypass channel
is proposed; the accepted offsite flow is passed through the onsite storm drain and routed through detention
along with the onsite runoff.
2.4 Downstream Conveyance
The shared onsite outfall is located at the southwest corner of the property and discharges to the downstream
regional CCRFCD facility via an existing reinforced concrete pipe stub set during earlier regional construction.
The receiving facility has been reviewed against the shared outfall allowance identified in Section 5; downstream
capacity is not the controlling constraint for the site's release rate. The controlling constraint is the outfall
allowance established for Desert Sage Ranch and set forth in this study.
3. HYDROLOGY
3.1 Design Storm
Design storm criteria applied in this study are drawn from the CCRFCD Hydrologic Criteria and Drainage Design
Manual applicable at the time of preparation. The following storms have been evaluated:
• 100-year, 6-hour storm — used for peak discharge estimation and storm drain sizing.
• 100-year, 24-hour storm — used for detention basin sizing (governing storage volume).
Rainfall depths applied are as follows (Enterprise sub-basin, CCRFCD atlas values at time of preparation):

3.2 Method
Rainfall-runoff modeling was performed using CCRFCD-accepted methods appropriate for a subdivision of this
size, applying the Green-Ampt infiltration approach for pervious surfaces and directly-connected impervious
modeling for developed areas. Sub-basin delineation follows the tributary breakdown described in Section 3.3.
Routing to and through the shared detention basin(s) was performed using the storage-indication method.
Impervious cover assumed at build-out reflects the approved half-acre residential lot type with associated street
and driveway coverage, streetscape landscape strips, and HOA common-area park.

3.4 Peak Discharge Summary — Fully Developed Conditions
Fully developed peak flows to the shared onsite detention basin(s), computed under the 100-year, 6-hour storm
inclusive of the accepted offsite tributary inflow at the northern boundary, are summarized in Appendix C. The
peak inflow at the shared basin(s) governs the storm drain sizing but does not govern the shared outfall release,
which is fixed by the allowance in Section 5.
4. DETENTION SIZING
4.1 Shared Onsite Detention Approach
Desert Sage Ranch is served by a shared onsite detention approach: the detention volume required to attenuate
the site's peak discharge to the accepted outfall release rate is provided in shared onsite detention facilities


--- page 6 ---
constructed as the subdivision phases advance. Detention basin locations are identified on the phasing exhibit
(Section 6).
The shared approach avoids duplication of small phase-scale basins and consolidates operations and
maintenance for the HOA. Because the phases share the same outfall and downstream facility, the storage
requirement has been determined for the fully developed 140-acre site and then allocated among the three
phases in accordance with the acreage and impervious cover of each phase.
4.2 Governing Design Storm
Storage sizing is governed by the 100-year, 24-hour design storm. The 100-year, 6-hour storm is used to check
peak discharge to the shared basin(s) and storm drain sizing, but does not govern storage. Storage-indication
routing under the 100-year, 24-hour storm, with the outfall released at the allowance identified in Section 5,
produces a total site-wide required storage volume of 16.4 acre-feet.
4.3 Detention Allocation by Phase
Total storage required for the fully developed 140-acre site is allocated to the three phases on the basis of
tributary runoff volume and position in the shared outfall, not by pro-rata acreage. Phase 3 discharges last
and carries the largest attenuation duty; volumes were reviewed and fixed at District acceptance, and are
the fixed planning basis for subsequent phase-level submittals.

5. OUTFALL
5.1 Shared Outfall
The full 140-acre Desert Sage Ranch subdivision discharges to the downstream regional CCRFCD facility
through a single shared outfall located at the southwest corner of the site. The outfall discharges via an existing
reinforced concrete pipe stub previously installed by others as part of regional drainage construction.
Confirmation of downstream capacity has been obtained from the District as part of this study's review.
5.2 Allowance and Cap
An allowance for the full 140 acres at the shared outfall to the downstream regional facility has been established
for Desert Sage Ranch, subject to the following cap:
Q100 ≤ 78 cfs at the shared outfall.
The 78 cfs cap represents the maximum permitted 100-year peak discharge from the fully developed 140-acre
site into the receiving regional facility. Storage-indication routing through the shared onsite detention basin(s) as
sized in Section 4 attenuates the fully developed peak inflow at the basin(s) to a peak release at or below the 78
cfs cap.
5.3 Application to Phase-Level Plans
Because the cap applies to the shared outfall for the full 140-acre site — not to any single phase — phase-level
improvement plan sets are not to compute a phase-specific outfall discharge. Each phase's contribution is
routed into the shared detention system, and the shared outfall discharge remains subject to the 78 cfs cap at
build-out.
6. PHASING EXHIBIT
The Phasing Exhibit, provided as Appendix E and reproduced at reduced scale below, identifies:
• The three phase boundaries — Phase 1 (northern), Phase 2 (central), and Phase 3 (southern) —
comprising the 140-acre site.
• The location of the shared onsite detention basin(s) serving the subdivision.
• The offsite tributary corridor along the northern site boundary.
• The shared outfall at the southwest corner of the site and its connection to the downstream regional
CCRFCD facility.
• The phase-boundary storm drain interconnections that link each phase's contributory area to the shared
detention system.


--- page 8 ---
The exhibit is drawn at 1"=200′ on a 24×36 sheet; reference should be made to the full-size exhibit in Appendix
E for construction of phase-level improvement plans. Phase-level plans shall reflect the boundaries and basin
locations shown on the exhibit; deviations require formal amendment as set forth in Section 7.
(Phasing Exhibit — see Appendix E.)
7. CONCLUSION
7.1 Summary
This Master Drainage Study establishes the hydrologic and hydraulic basis of design for the 140-acre Desert
Sage Ranch subdivision. The study:
• adopts the 100-year, 6-hour and 100-year, 24-hour design storms in accordance with the CCRFCD
Hydrologic Criteria and Drainage Design Manual applicable at time of preparation;
• delineates tributary areas for the full 140 acres, broken down by the three development phases;
• establishes a shared onsite detention approach with fixed volume allocations by phase — Phase 1 at 4.2
acre-feet, Phase 2 at 5.8 acre-feet, Phase 3 at 6.4 acre-feet, and total site at 16.4 acre-feet;
• confirms an allowance for the full 140 acres at the shared outfall to the downstream regional facility,
capped at Q100 = 78 cfs;
• provides a phasing exhibit identifying phase boundaries, detention basin locations, offsite tributary corridor
and shared outfall.
7.2 Basis for Subsequent Design
Upon CCRFCD acceptance, this Master Drainage Study serves as the master planning document for all
subsequent improvement plan submittals for Desert Sage Ranch, including but not limited to Phase 1, Phase 2
and Phase 3 grading and drainage plan sets and their supporting hydrology, storm drain and detention
worksheets. Phase-level design shall be consistent with the tributary breakdown, detention allocation by phase,
and shared outfall allowance identified herein.
7.3 Amendments
Changes to the accepted detention allocations set forth in Table 4-1, the outfall allowance set forth in Section 5,
or the tributary breakdown and phase boundaries set forth in Sections 3 and 6, require formal amendment to this
study and re-review by the Clark County Regional Flood Control District. Phase-level improvement plans that
propose to depart from the accepted allocations or allowance shall be preceded by an accepted amendment; no
phase-level plan set shall be approved on the basis of a departure that has not been separately submitted to
and accepted by the District.
The CCRFCD acceptance letter dated February 28, 2022 (Appendix F) confirms this requirement and is
incorporated herein by reference.

profile view that the sewer is the lower utility and shall be encased where separation is less than 18 inches.

recommendation of 3.0" AC over 6.0" ATB over 12" Type II. Confirm the pavement callout and add a reference

RECORDING REQUESTED BY AND WHEN RECORDED RETURN TO:
Vogel & Marsh LLP Attn: Adrienne Vogel, Esq. (NV Bar #10412) 3960 Howard Hughes Parkway, Suite 900 Las
Vegas, NV 89169
APN(s): 177-27-201-001 and consecutively assigned lot and parcel numbers within the recorded plat of Desert
Sage Ranch.
Recorded: December 23, 2024 Instrument No. 20241223-0004422 Book 175, Page 61, Official Records, Clark
County, Nevada
(Space above this line reserved for Recorder's use)
DECLARATION OF COVENANTS, CONDITIONS, AND RESTRICTIONS
FOR DESERT SAGE RANCH
WITH COMMON AREA MAINTENANCE EXHIBIT
THIS DECLARATION OF COVENANTS, CONDITIONS, AND RESTRICTIONS FOR DESERT SAGE RANCH
(this "Declaration") is made and executed this 23rd day of December, 2024, by CALLAWAY LAND PARTNERS,
a Nevada limited liability company, having a principal place of business at 8880 W. Sunset Road, Suite 400, Las
Vegas, NV 89148 (the "Declarant"), with reference to the facts recited below.
ARTICLE I. RECITALS
A. Declarant is the owner in fee simple of certain real property situated in the unincorporated area of Clark
County, Nevada, being a portion of Section 27, Township 22 South, Range 60 East, M.D.M., Clark County,
Nevada, consisting of approximately 140.0 acres and commonly known and identified as the Desert Sage
Ranch subdivision (the "Property").
B. Declarant has caused the Property to be subdivided into three (3) sequential phases, being Phase 1, Phase
2, and Phase 3, together comprising residential lots, common-area parcels, streetscape parcels, and dedicated
public rights-of-way, all as more particularly depicted on the recorded final map(s) of the Property.
C. Concurrently with the execution and recordation of this Declaration, the First Final Map for Desert Sage
Ranch, Phases 1 and 2, being Map No. NFM-24-0118, is being recorded in the Office of the Clark County
Recorder at Book 175, Page 60 of Official Records ("First Final Map"). This Declaration is intended to be
recorded contemporaneously with, and to encumber the property depicted upon, the First Final Map, and to run
with and encumber the entire Property, including the Phase 3 remainder to be depicted on a successive final
map, upon its recordation.
D. It is the intention of Declarant to establish and impose upon the Property a general plan for the improvement,
protection, maintenance, and administration of Desert Sage Ranch as a planned residential community,
including without limitation the ownership and maintenance of certain common areas by a community
association formed for that purpose.


--- page 2 ---
E. Declarant intends that the covenants, conditions, restrictions, easements, assessments, charges, and liens
set forth below shall run with the land and be binding upon all persons or entities having or acquiring any right,
title, or interest in the Property or any portion thereof, and shall inure to the benefit of each Owner thereof.
F. Declarant has caused this Declaration to be prepared by Adrienne Vogel, Esq., of Vogel & Marsh LLP,
outside counsel to Declarant, in the manner set forth herein.
NOW, THEREFORE, Declarant hereby declares that the Property shall be held, sold, conveyed, encumbered,
hypothecated, leased, used, occupied, and improved subject to the following covenants, conditions, restrictions,
easements, assessments, charges, and liens, all of which are declared to be in furtherance of a general plan
and scheme for the subdivision, improvement, and sale of the Property.
ARTICLE II. DEFINITIONS
The following capitalized terms, when used in this Declaration, shall have the meanings set forth in this Article II.
Terms not otherwise defined herein shall have the meanings customarily ascribed to them under Chapter 116 of
the Nevada Revised Statutes.
Section 2.1. "Articles." The Articles of Incorporation of the Association, as the same may be amended from
time to time.
Section 2.2. "Association." Desert Sage Ranch Community Association, a Nevada nonprofit corporation,
being the community association formed by Declarant to administer, own, and maintain the Common Area and
to enforce the terms of this Declaration. The Association is the community association contemplated by NRS
Chapter 116. All references herein to "HOA" mean the Association.
Section 2.3. "Board." The Board of Directors of the Association.
Section 2.4. "Bylaws." The Bylaws of the Association, as the same may be amended from time to time.
Section 2.5. "Common Area." All real property (including any Improvements thereon) that is (i) owned by the
Association in fee simple, or (ii) held by the Association under an easement, license, or maintenance obligation
for the common use and enjoyment of the Owners. Common Area expressly includes, without limitation, the
Common-Area Park, the Streetscape Common Area, the Entry Feature, and all landscaping, irrigation
infrastructure, hardscape, walls, monumentation, signage, and amenities located therein as installed by
Declarant or its successors. Common Area does not include any Lot or any portion of a public right-of-way
conveyed by dedication to Clark County or another public body.
Section 2.6. "Common-Area Park." The parcel of Common Area designated on the recorded final map as
Parcel A, being an active-use park parcel improved with landscaping, irrigation, and, as installed by Declarant,
any turf area and any playground amenities (which, where installed, may consist of slides, swings, and climbing
structures). Parcel A is owned by the Association and is not part of any Lot.
Section 2.7. "Declarant." Callaway Land Partners, a Nevada limited liability company, and its successors and
assigns to whom the rights of Declarant hereunder are expressly assigned in a recorded instrument.
Section 2.8. "Declaration." This Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions for Desert Sage
Ranch, together with all exhibits and attachments hereto and all amendments and supplements duly recorded.


--- page 3 ---
Section 2.9. "Entry Feature." The parcel of Common Area designated on the recorded final map as Parcel C,
being the community entry treatment situated at the intersection of Rainbow Boulevard and Windmill Lane, and
improved with entry monumentation, signage, walls, planting, irrigation, and accent lighting. Parcel C is owned
by the Association and is not part of any Lot.
Section 2.10. "Governing Documents." This Declaration, the Articles, the Bylaws, and the rules and
regulations of the Association, each as the same may be amended from time to time, together with all recorded
exhibits, plats, and supplemental declarations.
Section 2.11. "Improvement." Any structure, wall, fence, monument, sign, tree, shrub, turf, planting, irrigation
line, playground amenity, path, hardscape, or other tangible thing installed upon or affixed to the land.
Section 2.12. "Lot." Each numbered residential lot depicted upon a recorded final map of the Property and
intended for the construction and occupancy of a single detached residential dwelling. Each Lot is a separately
conveyable parcel; no Lot includes any portion of any Common Area, and no Common Area is any part of any
Lot.
Section 2.13. "Managing Agent." The community management firm engaged by the Association pursuant to a
written management agreement to perform the day-to-day administration of the Association's affairs, including
the maintenance and replacement obligations set forth in Article V. As of the date of this Declaration, the
Managing Agent is Sagebrook Community Management LLC, a Nevada limited-liability company, having offices
at 6280 S. Pecos Road, Suite 300, Las Vegas, NV 89120.
Section 2.14. "Map" or "Final Map." Any final subdivision map of any portion of the Property recorded in the
Office of the Clark County Recorder, including the First Final Map (Map No. NFM-24-0118, recorded at Book
175, Page 60) and any successive final map for Phase 3.
Section 2.15. "Owner." The record holder of fee simple title to a Lot, excluding any person or entity holding title
solely as security for the performance of an obligation.
Section 2.16. "Property." All of the real property described in Article III below and shown upon the Map(s),
together with all Improvements thereon, and any additional property annexed hereto in accordance with this
Declaration.
Section 2.17. "Streetscape Common Area." Those parcels or strips of Common Area situated between the
back-of-curb of a public street and the front or side lot lines of the adjoining Lots (or, where applicable, between
the back-of-curb and a perimeter community wall), extending along all frontage of the Property, and improved
with sidewalks (where the sidewalk is not within the dedicated public right-of-way), desert planting, street trees,
and drip irrigation. Each Streetscape Common Area parcel is owned by the Association and is not part of any
Lot.
ARTICLE III. PROPERTY DESCRIPTION
Section 3.1. Legal Description of the Property. The Property subject to this Declaration is that certain real
property situated in the unincorporated area of Clark County, State of Nevada, more particularly described as
follows:
A portion of Section 27, Township 22 South, Range 60 East, M.D.M., Clark County, Nevada,
containing approximately 140.0 acres, together with all easements, tenements, hereditaments, and
appurtenances thereunto belonging, commonly known as Desert Sage Ranch, situated at the
intersection of Rainbow Boulevard and Windmill Lane, Las Vegas, Nevada 89178.


--- page 4 ---
Section 3.2. Phasing. The Property is subject to development in three sequential phases:
(a) Phase 1 — as more particularly depicted upon the First Final Map (Map No. NFM-24-0118, Book 175, Page
60), consisting of residential Lots, streetscape and open-space Common Area, and dedicated street
rights-of-way, all as shown upon Sheets 2 through 4 of the First Final Map.
(b) Phase 2 — as more particularly depicted upon the First Final Map (Map No. NFM-24-0118, Book 175, Page
60), consisting of residential Lots, streetscape and open-space Common Area (including the Common-Area
Park designated Parcel A, the shared Detention Facility designated Parcel B, and the Entry Feature designated
Parcel C), and dedicated street rights-of-way, all as shown upon Sheets 2 through 4 of the First Final Map.
(c) Phase 3 — that portion of the Property consisting of approximately 40.0 acres, presently identified by Clark
County Assessor's Parcel Number 177-27-201-001, to be subdivided into approximately sixty (60) half-acre
residential Lots, together with associated streetscape Common Area and dedicated street rights-of-way, all to be
depicted upon a successive final map to be recorded by Declarant. Upon recordation of the Phase 3 final map,
the Lots and Common Area created thereby shall automatically be and become subject to this Declaration
without the necessity of any further instrument.
Section 3.3. Annexation of Successive Phases. Declarant reserves the right, exercisable in its sole discretion
and without the consent of any Owner, Mortgagee, or the Association, to annex Phase 3 (and any lawful
reconfiguration thereof) to the regime of this Declaration by recordation of a Supplemental Declaration in the
Office of the Clark County Recorder that (i) identifies the annexed property by reference to the recorded final
map, and (ii) states that the annexed property is thereby made subject to this Declaration.
Section 3.4. Public Rights-of-Way. All streets, alleys, and other public rights-of-way depicted upon any Map
are conveyed by dedication to Clark County or the applicable public body. No such dedicated area is Common
Area, and the Association bears no maintenance obligation for improvements accepted for public maintenance
within any such dedicated area, except as provided by written agreement with the applicable public body.
ARTICLE IV. COMMON AREAS
Section 4.1. Establishment of Common Area. Declarant hereby establishes and dedicates for the common
use and enjoyment of the Owners, and conveys to the Association concurrently herewith and by the recordation
of each applicable Map, all Common Area, in fee simple, free and clear of all monetary encumbrances other
than the lien of current taxes and assessments not yet delinquent and matters of record specifically noted upon
the Map.
Section 4.2. Parcel A — Common-Area Park. The parcel designated Parcel A on the First Final Map (and as
reflected in Exhibit B hereto) is hereby established as the Common-Area Park. Parcel A is owned in fee simple
by the Association and is not part of any Lot. Parcel A is improved by Declarant with landscaping, irrigation, and,
as installed by Declarant, any turf area and any playground amenities (which, where installed by Declarant, may
consist of slides, swings, and climbing structures). All landscaping, irrigation infrastructure, turf, planting,
hardscape, and playground amenities installed upon Parcel A, as and where installed, constitute Common Area
Improvements owned by the Association.
Section 4.3. Parcel C — Entry Feature. The parcel designated Parcel C on the First Final Map (and as
reflected in Exhibit B hereto) is hereby established as the Entry Feature. Parcel C is owned in fee simple by the
Association and is not part of any Lot. Parcel C is improved by Declarant with community entry monumentation,
community identification signage, decorative perimeter walls, drip-irrigated desert planting, and accent lighting.
All Improvements installed upon Parcel C constitute Common Area Improvements owned by the Association.


--- page 5 ---
Section 4.4. Streetscape Common Area. The streetscape strips depicted on each recorded Map along all
frontage of the Property, being situated between the back-of-curb of the adjoining public street and the front or
side lot lines of the abutting Lots (or the adjoining perimeter wall, where applicable), are hereby established as
Streetscape Common Area. Each such strip is owned in fee simple by the Association, is not part of any Lot,
and is improved by Declarant with street trees, drip-irrigated desert planting, decorative rock cover, and, where
applicable, community perimeter wall and sidewalk. The Streetscape Common Area extends continuously along
the entire street frontage of the Property, in the extent depicted upon the First Final Map and upon any
successive final map recorded for Phase 3.
Section 4.5. Distinct from Lots. The Common-Area Park (Parcel A), the shared Detention Facility (Parcel B),
the Entry Feature (Parcel C), and each Streetscape Common Area parcel are each Common Area owned and
maintained by the Association, and no such parcel is a Lot or any part of a Lot. No Owner has any right, by
virtue of ownership of a Lot, to construct, remove, alter, replace, or reconfigure any Improvement located within
any Common Area.
Section 4.6. Easements Appurtenant. Every Owner shall have a nonexclusive easement of use and
enjoyment in and to the Common Area, appurtenant to and passing with title to such Owner's Lot, subject to the
terms of this Declaration and the rules and regulations of the Association.
Section 4.7. Reserved Easements. Declarant reserves to itself, the Association, the Managing Agent, and their
respective employees, agents, and contractors, a perpetual easement over, upon, across, and through each
Common Area parcel for the purposes of installing, inspecting, maintaining, repairing, and replacing Common
Area Improvements, including without limitation landscaping, irrigation infrastructure, turf, planting, and
playground amenities, as installed.
Section 4.8. No Partition. The Common Area shall remain undivided. No Owner or other person shall bring any
action for the partition or division of the Common Area, and each Owner waives any right of partition such
Owner may hold at law or in equity.
ARTICLE V. MAINTENANCE AND REPLACEMENT
Section 5.1. Association Responsibility. The Association shall be responsible for the continuous and ongoing
maintenance, repair, and replacement of the Common Area and all Improvements located thereon, including
without limitation:
(a) all landscaping within the Common Area, including all turf, planting, groundcover, shrubs, and trees, as and
where installed;
(b) all irrigation infrastructure within the Common Area, including without limitation mainline, laterals, valves,
valve boxes, backflow prevention assemblies, controllers, wiring, and emitters;
(c) all playground amenities located within the Common Area, as installed, including without limitation slides,
swings, climbing structures, and any associated resilient surfacing, safety zone materials, and containment
curbing;
(d) all hardscape within the Common Area, including sidewalks (where not within a dedicated public right-of-way
accepted for public maintenance), walls, monumentation, signage, benches, and accent lighting; and
(e) all other Improvements installed within the Common Area from time to time by Declarant or the Association.


--- page 6 ---
Section 5.2. Delegation to Managing Agent. The Association hereby delegates the day-to-day performance of
the maintenance, repair, and replacement obligations set forth in Section 5.1 to its Managing Agent, being, as of
the date of this Declaration, Sagebrook Community Management LLC, a Nevada limited-liability company
having offices at 6280 S. Pecos Road, Suite 300, Las Vegas, NV 89120. The Managing Agent shall perform
such obligations pursuant to and in accordance with the written management agreement entered into between
the Association and the Managing Agent (the "Management Agreement"), which Management Agreement may
be renewed, replaced, or terminated by the Board in accordance with its terms and applicable law.
Section 5.3. Scope of Managing Agent Obligation. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, the
Managing Agent is charged with and shall perform, in the name and on behalf of the Association:
(a) all routine and non-routine maintenance, repair, and replacement of the landscaping within all Common Area
parcels, including any turf, any planting, and any irrigation infrastructure, as and where installed by Declarant or
subsequently installed by or on behalf of the Association;
(b) the maintenance, repair, and replacement of all playground amenities located within any Common Area
parcel, as and where installed, including inspection for safety compliance and the replacement of resilient
surfacing and impact-attenuating materials;

Meeting date: 06/22/2026

Name | Affiliation | Role | Present
Max Braddock | Sundial Engineering & Survey | Project Manager | In person

Lt. R. Salazar | Clark County Fire Department | Fire Plans review (alternate for Capt. Roark) | In person
K. Odhiambo | Clark County Development Services | Utilities coordination | In person

Callaway Land Partners was invited but did not attend; Max Braddock represented applicant-side coordination.
2. Purpose
Pre-application discussion of the Desert Sage Ranch Phase 3 improvement plan and final map resubmittal package under the current code cycle. Objective was to align the design team and County reviewers on submittal composition, review path, and any threshold issues that ought to be flagged before intake, so the package can move through Public Works plan check on the first submittal without a routing surprise.
Phase 3 is the final 40.0 acres (60 half-acre lots) of the 140-acre subdivision entitled under Tentative Map TM-22-500041 (approved 03/14/2022). Phases 1 and 2 are built and occupied; the first final map in the series was recorded in 2024.
3. Topics Discussed
3.1 Submittal package composition and application numbers. Max walked through the intended package. County has already issued application numbers on the intake pre-check:
Improvement Plans: IP-26-100288
Final Map: FM-26-100290
Package as contemplated for first submittal:
Improvement plan set (grading, drainage, streets, wet/dry utility composite) — Sundial
Landscape and irrigation set — Ocotillo Landscape Studio
Final Map (three-sheet, second in the TM-22-500041 series) — Sundial Survey
Supporting reports: updated drainage narrative referencing the approved master drainage study; geotechnical addendum; traffic memo confirming trip generation is unchanged from tentative-map assumptions
Title report and closure package — Callaway to procure through Silver Butte Title & Escrow
Agency will-serve / capacity confirmations from LVVWD and CCWRD (see 3.5)
Dale Yeoman confirmed the two application numbers above are the correct references and should appear on the title block and cover sheets of every submitted sheet. He asked that IP-26-100288 be cited on the drainage narrative title page as well.
3.2 Drainage — master study governs. Priya summarized the drainage approach: Phase 3 drains to the detention basin sized under the approved master drainage study for the subdivision. Detention allocation for Phase 3 was fixed in that study; there are no departures anticipated in the resubmittal.
Dale confirmed that so long as the Phase 3 improvement plans match the volumes and outfall configuration in the district-approved master drainage study, no fresh hydrology submittal to Regional Flood Control is required — a narrative-level reconciliation in the drainage report is sufficient. He noted plan check will still verify the basin geometry against the study.
Priya to include a reconciliation table (basin volume as built into Phase 1/2, allocations for Phase 3, and headroom) in the drainage narrative.
3.3 Landscape — significant-change threshold. Bea Cortland summarized the landscape approach: streetscape palette carried forward from the approved 2022 Phase 1/2 palette (desert planting throughout streetscapes; turf confined to the HOA common-area park). Species list is substantially the same as Phase 1/2. Some substitutions in the shrub layer may be proposed as availability has shifted since 2022.
Odette Marchetti raised that any landscape changes from the approved 2022 palette may require review beyond staff level depending on extent — the significant-change threshold has to be evaluated on the actual proposed change. She referenced condition 14 of the tentative map approval letter, which contemplates design review as a public hearing before the Town Advisory Board and Planning Commission for significant changes to approved plans, including landscape and streetscape treatments in common areas.
Discussion did not resolve where the significant-change threshold sits for this project. Odette noted the evaluation is fact-specific and that the design team should provide a red-line comparison of the proposed Phase 3 palette against the 2022 approved palette so Planning can make that call once the actual proposed change is on paper. Bea agreed to prepare that comparison as part of the landscape resubmittal.
No commitment was made at the meeting as to whether the resubmittal will or will not trigger design review. The point was flagged for the team's awareness; a written determination from Planning would follow the submittal.
3.4 Fire access. Lt. Salazar (attending for Capt. Roark) noted that the CCFD review will focus on the permanent buildout access configuration for Phase 3. The temporary secondary access accepted at Phase 2 buildout was approved as a temporary condition pending Phase 3 development, and Phase 3 improvement plans need to show the permanent second point of access consistent with the tentative map. Any deviation from what was shown on TM-22-500041 should be pre-coordinated with Capt. Roark before submittal.
Sundial to circulate the current Phase 3 access layout to CCFD in advance of the formal submittal for informal review; the substantive determination on the permanent buildout condition will come from CCFD through the plan check letter.
3.5 Utilities. K. Odhiambo confirmed that separate confirmations from Las Vegas Valley Water District (LVVWD) and Clark County Water Reclamation District (CCWRD) will be needed for the resubmittal package. These are separate agency confirmations obtained by the applicant/engineer directly with each district; the County does not procure them.
Noted for the record; no further discussion.
3.6 SWPPP / grading permit sequencing. Priya asked about sequencing between improvement plan approval and the grading permit / SWPPP. Dale confirmed the standard sequence:
Improvement plans routed and approved (IP-26-100288)
NDEP Bureau of Water Pollution Control NOI filed by contractor; SWPPP prepared under NPDES general construction permit
Grading permit application submitted to Public Works with the SWPPP and approved improvement plans referenced
Grading permit issued once bonds/estimate are posted through Callaway
The grading permit cannot issue ahead of improvement plan approval. Dale mentioned that Callaway will need to have the surety and cost estimate lined up on the Public Works side before grading permit issuance, but that this is not a first-submittal item.
4. Agreed Submittal Route
The resubmittal will be routed through Clark County Public Works, Development Review, with Comprehensive Planning coordination on the landscape and final map conditions. Dale Yeoman is the assigned civil plans examiner (Public Works). Odette Marchetti is the point of contact on the Comprehensive Planning side for the tentative map conditions carry-forward and the significant-change evaluation.
Public Works will circulate the improvement plans internally to CCFD and Landscape review. Applicant is responsible for obtaining LVVWD and CCWRD confirmations separately (see 3.5) and including them in the submittal package.
Formal intake will be at the Public Works counter under application numbers IP-26-100288 (improvement plans) and FM-26-100290 (final map).
5. Action Items

1 | Prepare improvement plan set, drainage narrative reconciliation, and final map for first submittal | Sundial (Braddock / Sarwal) | Advance of submittal
2 | Circulate current Phase 3 permanent-access layout to CCFD (Capt. Roark) for informal pre-review | Sundial (Braddock) | Ahead of formal submittal
3 | Update Phase 3 landscape and irrigation sheets against the 2022 approved palette; prepare red-line comparison for Planning | Ocotillo (Cortland) | Advance of submittal
4 | Procure updated preliminary title report and closure package for the Phase 3 final map | Callaway (title order through Silver Butte Title & Escrow) | Advance of submittal
5 | Obtain current LVVWD and CCWRD confirmations for inclusion in the submittal package | Sundial (Braddock) with Callaway | Advance of submittal
6 | Confirm bond/estimate posting path with Public Works ahead of grading permit application | Callaway (Nokes) | Post-IP approval

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""AHPELE requirement scanner (stdlib only; runs inside the task container).

Finds requirement-like statements in the text corpus written by
ahpele_index.py (/tmp/ahpele/corpus) so that hard constraints are not missed:

  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py            # scan: writes /tmp/ahpele/req_candidates.md and .csv
  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py --check    # coverage: lists candidates not yet reviewed
  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py --register FILE.csv|.xlsx   # register rows: is each value in the document it cites?

A candidate counts as reviewed when its ID (e.g. R0042) appears in
/tmp/ahpele/requirements.csv (adopted) or /tmp/ahpele/rejected.csv (rejected,
with a reason). A whole document can be rejected by putting its path in
rejected.csv. The scanner is a recall aid: it misses requirements that live in
tables, drawings or images, and it lists many statements that are not hard
requirements. It knows nothing about any particular task.
"""
import argparse
import csv
import html
import json
import os
import re
import sys

OUT = "/tmp/ahpele"
STRONG = re.compile(
    r"\b(shall|must|is required|are required|required to|mandatory|not permitted|prohibited|shall not|"
    r"must not|may not exceed|no later than|condition of|subject to|is to|are to|(is|are)? ?limited to|"
    r"not (be )?(less|more|greater|lower|higher) than|not exceed|at least|at most|no more than|no less than|"
    r"maximum of|minimum of|is not allowed|are not allowed|will not be accepted|not acceptable)\b", re.I)
LIMIT = re.compile(
    r"(\b(not (to )?exceed|exceed(s|ing)?|maximum|minimum|max\.?|min\.?|at least|at most|no more than|"
    r"no less than|not less than|not more than|not greater than|up to|limit(ed|s)?|cap(ped)?|allowable|"
    r"permissible|permitted|threshold|tolerance|deadline|before|prior to|within|until|expires?|valid)\b|"
    r"[≤≥<>]=?|±|\+/-)", re.I)
NUMBER = re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z])[-+]?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?")
NOISE = re.compile(r"^(--- page \d+ ---|page \d+( of \d+)?|\W*)$", re.I)
MAX_LEN = 320
TAG = re.compile(r"<[^<>]{1,400}>")
# folders that usually hold general reference material (codes, standards, catalogues) rather than project documents
REFERENCE = re.compile(r"(^|/)(library|libraries|reference|references|standards?|codes?|regulations?|catalogues?|"
                       r"catalogs?|vendor|manufacturer)(/|$)", re.I)
# file names of published codes and standards (general engineering knowledge, not task-specific)
STANDARD_NAME = re.compile(
    r"^(\d+[ _-]?CFR|UFC|UFGS|UFM|ASCE|SEI|ACI|AISC|AISI|SDI|SJI|IBC|IRC|IFC[ _-]?\d|IECC|IEC|IEEE|NFPA|NEC|NESC|ISO|EN|"
    r"BS|ASTM|ASHRAE|ASME|AWS|AWWA|API|ANSI|UL|CSA|DIN|AS|NZS|TIA|FM|NEMA|OSHA|EPA|FEMA|AASHTO|MUTCD|ICC|NCHRP|"
    r"USACE|EM[ _-]\d|ETL|DoD|IS)[ _-]?\d", re.I)
DATA_TYPES = {"csv", "json"}
VOID_DIR = re.compile(r"(^|/)(archive[sd]?|superseded|obsolete|old|void|withdrawn|cancell?ed)(/|$)", re.I)


def load_inventory():
    try:
        with open(os.path.join(OUT, "inventory.json"), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            return {r["path"]: r for r in json.load(fh).get("files", [])}
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return {}


def statements(text):
    """Yield (page, statement) pairs: lines joined into sentences, table rows kept whole."""
    page, buf = 1, []
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        m = re.match(r"--- page (\d+) ---", raw.strip())
        if m:
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            page = int(m.group(1))
            continue
        line = raw.strip()
        if NOISE.match(line):
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            continue
        if "\t" in raw or " | " in line or line.count("  ") > 2:  # table-like row
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            yield page, re.sub(r"\s+", " ", line)
            continue
        buf.append(line)
        if re.search(r"[.;:]$", line) or len(" ".join(buf)) > 600:
            yield page, " ".join(buf)
            buf = []
    if buf:
        yield page, " ".join(buf)


def split_sentences(s):
    parts = re.split(r"(?<=[.;])\s+(?=[A-Z(])", s)
    return [p.strip() for p in parts if p.strip()]


def scan():
    corpus = os.path.join(OUT, "corpus")
    inv = load_inventory()
    rows = []
    data_like = {d for d, r in inv.items() if r.get("type") in DATA_TYPES}
    for dp, _, fns in os.walk(corpus):
        for fn in sorted(fns):
            if not fn.endswith(".txt"):
                continue
            full = os.path.join(dp, fn)
            doc = os.path.relpath(full, corpus)[:-4]
            try:
                text = open(full, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
            except OSError:
                continue
            if text.count("<") > 20 and len(TAG.findall(text[:20000])) > 20:  # XML / HTML: keep the text only
                text = html.unescape(TAG.sub(lambda m: "\n" if re.match(r"</?(p|div|tr|li|h\d|head|br|section|para)\b",
                                                                     m.group(0), re.I) else " ", text))
            seen = set()
            for page, st in statements(text):
                for s in split_sentences(st):
                    strong, limit, nums = bool(STRONG.search(s)), bool(LIMIT.search(s)), NUMBER.findall(s)
                    if not (strong or (limit and nums)) or (doc in data_like and not strong):
                        continue
                    key = s.lower()[:200]
                    if key in seen or len(s) < 12:
                        continue
                    seen.add(key)
                    score = (4 if nums else 3) if strong else 2  # 4: modal + number, 3: modal, 2: limit + number
                    rows.append({"doc": doc, "page": page, "score": score,
                                 "text": s if len(s) <= MAX_LEN else s[:MAX_LEN] + "…",
                                 "numbers": " ".join(nums[:8])})
    for r in rows:
        r["ref"] = bool(REFERENCE.search(os.path.dirname(r["doc"]))
                        or STANDARD_NAME.search(os.path.basename(r["doc"])))
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: (r["ref"], r["doc"], r["page"]))
    for i, r in enumerate(rows, 1):
        r["id"] = f"R{i:04d}"
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.csv"), "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=["id", "doc", "page", "score", "ref", "numbers", "text"])
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)
    by_doc = {}
    for r in rows:
        by_doc.setdefault(r["doc"], []).append(r)
    lines = ["# Requirement candidates", "",
             f"{len(rows)} requirement-like statements in {len(by_doc)} documents (score 4: shall/must/"
             "not-more-than wording with a number; 3: the same wording without a number; 2: a limit word with a "
             "number, often context rather than a requirement). Tables, drawings and scanned pages are only partly covered: "
             "read those yourself. Status flags come from the FILE NAME; confirm which documents govern. Project "
             "documents come first; published codes and standards and documents in reference folders are listed "
             "last: the clauses that apply are the ones the project documents invoke. --check asks you to review the "
             "score 3-4 statements of project documents; use the rest when you look a requirement up.", ""]
    shown_ref = False
    for doc, rs in by_doc.items():
        if rs[0]["ref"] and not shown_ref:
            lines += ["# Reference folders (codes, standards, catalogues)", ""]
            shown_ref = True
        flags = inv.get(doc, {}).get("flags", "")
        lines.append(f"## {doc}" + (f"  [name flags: {flags}]" if flags else "") + f"  ({len(rs)})")
        for r in rs:
            lines.append(f"- {r['id']} p{r['page']} s{r['score']}: {r['text']}")
        lines.append("")
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    key = [r for r in rows if must_review(r)]
    kdocs = {}
    for r in key:
        kdocs[r["doc"]] = kdocs.get(r["doc"], 0) + 1
    top = sorted(kdocs.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:10]
    print(f"requirement scan: {len(rows)} candidates in {len(by_doc)} documents -> {OUT}/req_candidates.md; "
          f"{len(key)} strong candidates in project documents to review"
          + (" (" + ", ".join(f"{d}: {n}" for d, n in top) + ")" if top else ""))
    return rows


def must_review(r):
    """Requirement wording (shall, must, is to, not more than ...) in project documents."""
    return int(r["score"]) >= 3 and str(r["ref"]) not in ("True", "1")


def read_text(path):
    try:
        return open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
    except OSError:
        return ""


def check(limit):
    path = os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.csv")
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        scan()
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(fh))
    adopted = read_text(os.path.join(OUT, "requirements.csv"))
    rejected = read_text(os.path.join(OUT, "rejected.csv"))
    if not adopted.strip():
        print(f"{OUT}/requirements.csv is missing or empty: build the requirements table first "
              "(one row per hard requirement, with the candidate IDs it comes from).")
    ids = set(re.findall(r"\bR\d{4}\b", adopted + "\n" + rejected))
    rejected_docs = {r["doc"] for r in rows if r["doc"] in rejected}
    inv = load_inventory()
    key = [r for r in rows if must_review(r)]

    def covered(r):
        if r["id"] in ids:
            return True
        if r["doc"] not in rejected_docs:
            return False
        # rejecting a whole document covers its statements with a number only when the document is marked void
        # (status word in its file name, or an archive / superseded folder); otherwise each one needs its own ID
        return int(r["score"]) < 4 or bool(inv.get(r["doc"], {}).get("flags")) or bool(VOID_DIR.search(r["doc"]))

    open_rows = [r for r in key if not covered(r)]
    open_rows.sort(key=lambda r: (-int(r["score"]), r["doc"], int(r["page"])))
    n = len(key)
    print(f"coverage: {n - len(open_rows)}/{n} strong project-document candidates reviewed "
          f"({len(ids & {r['id'] for r in rows})} IDs cited in all, {len(rejected_docs)} documents rejected whole); "
          f"{len(open_rows)} not reviewed yet. ({len(rows) - n} weaker or code/standard candidates are optional: "
          f"see {OUT}/req_candidates.md.)")
    if not open_rows:
        print("Every candidate is adopted or rejected. Also check tables, drawings and scanned pages, which the "
              "scanner does not fully cover.")
        return 0
    print("Unreviewed candidates, strongest first (add each hard requirement to requirements.csv citing its ID, or "
          "list the ID with a reason in rejected.csv; a statement with a number in a document that is not marked "
          "void needs its own ID even if you rejected the document):")
    for r in open_rows[:limit]:
        print(f"- {r['id']} [{r['doc']} p{r['page']} s{r['score']}] {r['text'][:220]}")
    if len(open_rows) > limit:
        by = {}
        for r in open_rows[limit:]:
            by[r["doc"]] = by.get(r["doc"], 0) + 1
        print(f"... and {len(open_rows) - limit} more: " + ", ".join(f"{d} ({c})" for d, c in sorted(by.items())))
    return 1


SRC_COL = re.compile(r"source|clause|document|doc\b|ref|citation|basis|standard|section", re.I)
VAL_COL = re.compile(r"value|limit|threshold|criterion|criteria|requirement|min|max|allow", re.I)
CLAUSE_REF = re.compile(r"(§\s*[\w.()-]+|\b(?:clause|section|sec\.|para\.?|table|article|art\.)\s*[\w.()-]+)", re.I)


def norm_num(x):
    x = x.replace(",", "")
    try:
        v = float(x)
    except ValueError:
        return {x}
    out = {x, f"{v:g}"}
    if v == int(v):
        out.add(str(int(v)))
    return out


def read_register(path):
    if path.lower().endswith((".xlsx", ".xlsm")):
        try:
            import openpyxl
        except ImportError:
            sys.exit("--register on .xlsx needs openpyxl; export the sheet to CSV")
        wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(path, data_only=True, read_only=True)
        rows = []
        for ws in wb.worksheets:
            rows += [["" if c is None else str(c) for c in r] for r in ws.iter_rows(values_only=True)]

- The MDS amendment triggers are specific. [P0] SUNDIAL ENGINEERING & SURVEY

[P1] 4720 South Rainbow Boulevard, Suite 210  •  Las Vegas, Nevada 89103  •  (702) 555-0142  •  NV COA #C-3874

[P2] MEMORANDUM

[P4] 1. Bottom line

[P5] You asked whether the emergency spillway as drawn on C-9 holds up, whether G-4 can be answered from the current sheet, whether the correction triggers an amendment to the accepted Master Drainage Study, what the revised C-9 detail and basin notes must say, and where the overflow goes. Our answers are:

[P6] Answer 1 — G-4. The spillway as drawn does not hold up, and G-4 cannot be answered from C-9 as issued on 08/21/2026. The sheet shows a 20-ft-wide broad-crested weir but gives no design flow, no sizing calculation, no spillway section or freeboard dimension from the spillway design water surface, and no designed apron. At the accepted Phase 3 inflow of 88.4 cfs with the principal outlet blocked, the 20-ft weir requires 1.294793994 ft of head; only 0.70 ft is available between crest 2,858.50 ft and top of berm 2,859.20 ft. The design water surface is 2,859.794793994 ft, which overtops the berm by 0.594793994 ft. Even crediting the 41.5 cfs outlet discharge at the crest, the spillway would still overtop by 0.148557080 ft. The existing 15 ft by 20 ft grouted riprap apron with D50 = 12 in is also undersized for the calculated toe velocity of about 19.53 ft/s.

[P7] Answer 2 — Amendment. No formal amendment to the accepted Master Drainage Study is required for the G-4 correction. The 100-year water surface at 2,857.91 ft, the Phase 3 allocation of 6.4 acre-feet, the 40.0-acre/42% tributary basis, the Parcel E basin location, and the 78 cfs shared-outfall cap do not change. The correction is a plan-level C-9 detail. Because the top of berm moves from 2,859.20 ft to 2,860.80 ft, we will transmit the revised C-9 and spillway calculation to CCRFCD for concurrence under Condition 2 of the tentative map; that is a district concurrence, not a new hydrology study or an MDS amendment.

[P8] Answer 3 — Revised C-9. The revised C-9 must show a 36-ft minimum broad-crested weir at crest 2,858.50 ft, design Q = 88.4 cfs, head 0.875022069 ft, design WSE 2,859.375022069 ft, top of berm 2,860.80 ft, freeboard 1.424977931 ft at Q100 and 1.153396722 ft at 1.5Q = 132.6 cfs. The crest and chute should be 12 in by 18 in articulated concrete block over geotextile with cutoff walls, followed by a reinforced concrete stilling basin at least 20 ft long by 36 ft wide by 12 in thick with baffle blocks and an end sill, then 18-in D50 riprap at 27 in thick for 10 ft. The basin notes must correct the crest offset to 0.59 ft, state the design flow and spillway freeboard, and retain the 6.4 acre-feet allocation and the MDS reference.

[P9] Answer 4 — Overflow. Overflow leaves the east berm, crosses Common-Area Parcel E in an open swale to the Windmill Lane gutter line, and must then run west along Windmill Lane to the shared outfall at the southwest corner and the CCRFCD regional facility. The current record does not show a continuous swale alignment or inverts, a gutter capacity check, or a drainage easement. The revised C-9 must show the path wholly within Parcel E and public right-of-way, or add a drainage easement, and must demonstrate capacity. The emergency overflow is not routed through the 30-in principal outlet pipe.

[P10] 2. Purpose, records and governing basis

[P11] This memorandum is the engineering record of our review of the C-9 emergency spillway against the accepted Master Drainage Study (MDS), the Phase 3 improvement plans, the storm drain worksheets, the Phase 2 comments and the Clark County Regional Flood Control District (CCRFCD) acceptance letter. It answers CCPW comment G-4 in advance of assigning the detailed C-9 revision to the drainage lead. It does not replace the revised C-9, the spillway calculation sheet, or the CCRFCD concurrence.

[P12] The records relied on are listed below. Record abbreviations used in the rest of the memo are shown in brackets.

[P15] 3. Can G-4 be answered with what is on C-9 today?

[P16] No. C-9 as issued on 08/21/2026 identifies an emergency spillway and gives a few dimensions, but it does not contain the engineering content that G-4 requests. Specifically, the sheet does not give a design flow, a weir sizing calculation, a spillway section with headwater and tailwater, a freeboard dimension measured from the spillway design water surface, or an apron/erosion-protection design. The QA/QC checklist's statement that the weir detail is complete is incorrect (Section 9).

[P17] Table 3-1 lists what the sheet actually says. The values are taken directly from C-9 pages 17 and 18 and C-6 page 11.

[P18] Table 3-1 — Existing C-9 spillway data.

[P20] The 1.29 ft dimension in the basin notes is a 100-year-event freeboard, and it is correct as far as it goes. It is not the spillway freeboard. Because the crest is only 0.70 ft below the top of berm, any spillway flow consumes that 0.70 ft at a one-to-one rate. At the design flow the spillway design water surface is above the top of berm. A note that says the basin has 1.29 ft of freeboard at the 100-year water surface does not answer G-4 and does not make the spillway adequate.

[P21] 4. Spillway sizing — the 20-ft weir does not pass the design flow

[P22] 4.1 Design basis

[P23] The design storm for peak flow is the 100-year, 6-hour storm with a rainfall depth of 2.38 in (MDS Section 3.1, p.4, and Appendix A, p.10). The 100-year, 24-hour depth of 3.18 in governs detention storage volume, not peak spillway flow (MDS Section 4.2, p.6). The Phase 3 routed peak inflow to the shared detention basin is 88.4 cfs (MDS Appendix C, Table C-2, p.12; HYD Peak Flows, cell B13).

[P24] The arithmetic sum of the four Phase 3 sub-basin peaks is 96.8 cfs; after accounting for timing along the Phase 3 trunk, the combined inflow at the basin is 88.4 cfs (HYD Peak Flows, cells B12 and B13; MDS Appendix C, Table C-2, p.12).

[P25] The emergency spillway design flow is 88.4 cfs with the principal outlet assumed fully blocked. This is the conservative CCRFCD detention-basin check: the spillway must pass the unrouted 100-year inflow without credit for the outlet. We also checked 1.5 times the design flow, 132.6 cfs, so the selected geometry has reserve if the District requires a 1.5Q spillway check. Using the routed outflow of 27.9 cfs (MDS Appendix D-1, p.13) as the spillway design flow would under-size the spillway and is not accepted.

[P26] The weir is a broad-crested weir. In U.S. customary units:

[P27] Q = C · L · H^(3/2)

[P28] H = (Q / (C · L))^(2/3)

[P29] where Q is discharge in cubic feet per second, C is the broad-crested weir coefficient in ft^0.5/s, L is the crest length in feet, and H is the head above the crest in feet. We use C = 3.0 ft^0.5/s for a broad-crested concrete/articulated-block crest and check C = 2.6 ft^0.5/s as a conservative sensitivity. No intermediate value is rounded in the calculations below.

[P30] 4.2 Existing 20-ft weir at crest 2,858.50 ft

[P31] With L = 20 ft and C = 3.0 ft^0.5/s:

[P32] H = (88.4 / (3.0 × 20))^(2/3) = (1.473333333)^(2/3) = 1.294793994 ft

[P33] Design WSE = 2,858.50 + 1.294793994 = 2,859.794793994 ft

[P34] Available head to top of berm = 2,859.20 − 2,858.50 = 0.70 ft

[P35] Overtopping = 2,859.794793994 − 2,859.20 = 0.594793994 ft

[P36] The capacity of the 20-ft weir at the available 0.70 ft head is:

[P37] Q = 3.0 × 20 × (0.70)^(3/2) = 35.139721114 cfs

[P38] With the conservative C = 2.6 ft^0.5/s, the required head is 1.424402129 ft, the design WSE is 2,859.924402129 ft, and the overtopping is 0.724402129 ft. The capacity at 0.70 ft is 30.454424966 cfs. The crest length required to pass 88.4 cfs at 0.70 ft is 50.313432888 ft with C = 3.0, or 58.053961025 ft with C = 2.6. The 20-ft weir is less than half the required length.

[P39] Even if the outlet is credited at the crest, the check still fails. MDS Appendix D-2 gives 41.5 cfs outflow at elevation 2,858.50 ft. The spillway would then need to pass 88.4 − 41.5 = 46.9 cfs:

[P40] H = (46.9 / (3.0 × 20))^(2/3) = 0.848557080 ft

[P41] Design WSE = 2,858.50 + 0.848557080 = 2,859.348557080 ft

[P42] Overtopping = 2,859.348557080 − 2,859.20 = 0.148557080 ft

[P43] With C = 2.6, the credited-outlet head is 0.933497156 ft, the design WSE is 2,859.433497156 ft, and the overtopping is 0.233497156 ft. This is a conservative fixed-outlet credit at the crest; a coupled outlet/spillway rating would lower the water surface slightly as the outlet head rises, but it would not restore the 1.0-ft freeboard because the crest is only 0.70 ft below the top of berm. The conclusion is the same under either reading: the 20-ft spillway cannot pass the 100-year inflow within the available berm height, and it cannot provide the required freeboard.

[P44] 4.3 Required geometry for the revised C-9

[P45] The crest elevation of 2,858.50 ft is retained because it is 0.59 ft above the accepted 100-year water surface of 2,857.91 ft and is fixed in MDS Appendix D-2. The crest length is increased to 36 ft and the top of berm is raised to 2,860.80 ft. The 36-ft length is a practical multiple of the 18-in articulated-block width (24 blocks) and fits along the 195-ft east berm (C-6, p.11). The calculations are:

[P46] H at Q100 = (88.4 / (3.0 × 36))^(2/3) = 0.875022069 ft

[P47] Design WSE at Q100 = 2,858.50 + 0.875022069 = 2,859.375022069 ft

[P48] H at 1.5Q = (132.6 / (3.0 × 36))^(2/3) = 1.146603278 ft

[P49] Design WSE at 1.5Q = 2,858.50 + 1.146603278 = 2,859.646603278 ft

[P50] Freeboard at Q100 = 2,860.80 − 2,859.375022069 = 1.424977931 ft

[P51] Freeboard at 1.5Q = 2,860.80 − 2,859.646603278 = 1.153396722 ft

[P52] The conservative C = 2.6 check also passes: at Q100 the head is 0.962611275 ft, the design WSE is 2,859.462611275 ft, and the freeboard is 1.337388725 ft; at 1.5Q the head is 1.261377607 ft, the design WSE is 2,859.761377607 ft, and the freeboard is 1.038622393 ft. The 100-year freeboard to the new top of berm is 2,860.80 − 2,857.91 = 2.89 ft, and the crest-to-top dimension is 2,860.80 − 2,858.50 = 2.30 ft. Widening the weir alone is not sufficient: at Q100 the 36-ft design WSE of 2,859.375022069 ft is above the existing top of berm of 2,859.20 ft, so the top of berm must be raised to provide freeboard.

[P53] Table 4-1 — Spillway elevation stack (all elevations NAVD 88).

[P55] Table 4-2 — Spillway capacity and freeboard check. The table shows final values rounded to four decimal places; the unrounded values are in the calculation text above.

[P57] For completeness, the 36-ft weir also passes the arithmetic sum of the Phase 3 sub-basin peaks, 96.8 cfs: the head is 0.929610602 ft, the design WSE is 2,859.429610602 ft, and the freeboard to 2,860.80 ft is 1.370389398 ft. The 88.4 cfs timing-adjusted inflow remains the design basis.

[P58] Raising the top of berm by 1.60 ft is feasible within Parcel E. C-6 gives the basin top-of-berm footprint as approximately 293 ft by 195 ft, or 1.31 acres (C-6, p.11). The final map gives Parcel E as 2.04 acres (Final map, Sheet 4, 08/21/2026). With 4H:1V interior and 3H:1V exterior slopes, the top-of-berm footprint expands by roughly 0.15 acre, to about 1.46 acres, which remains inside the 2.04-acre parcel. The berm raise itself fits; the stilling basin, 10-ft riprap and overflow swale must also be shown inside Parcel E or within a drainage easement. The current C-6 does not dimension the east berm margin, so the revised C-6/C-9 must confirm that the 20-ft basin, the riprap and the swale fit. If they do not, the spillway must be shifted or an easement obtained; the basin and swale cannot be built outside Parcel E without an easement. All top-of-berm appurtenances must be raised with the berm, including the outlet headwall (currently top at 2,859.20 ft on C-9, p.18), the access gate and the perimeter maintenance path.

[P59] 4.4 Apron and erosion protection

[P60] The existing apron is 15 ft by 20 ft of grouted riprap with D50 = 12 in (C-9, p.17). It has no velocity basis. Using the existing 20-ft weir, the unit discharge at Q100 is 88.4/20 = 4.42 cfs/ft; critical depth is 0.846570029 ft and critical velocity is 5.221068370 ft/s. With a 5.5-ft drop from crest 2,858.50 ft to natural grade 2,853.00 ft, the ideal toe velocity is about 19.530989604 ft/s. For the proposed 36-ft weir, the unit discharge is 2.455555556 cfs/ft, critical depth is 0.572112213 ft, critical velocity is 4.292087285 ft/s, and the toe velocity is still about 19.303419730 ft/s because the drop dominates.

[P61] The Isbash riprap sizing check is:

[P62] D50 = V^2 / [2 · g · C^2 · (Gs − 1)]

[P63] With V = 19.530989604 ft/s, g = 32.2 ft/s^2, C = 0.86 for high turbulence, and Gs = 2.65, the required D50 is 4.853798953 ft, or 58.25 in. Reversing the equation, a 12-in D50 stone is adequate only to about 8.865094247 ft/s. The calculated toe velocity is more than twice that. A 12-in grouted riprap apron cannot be justified by calculation, and increasing the stone to a practical size is not the right solution at this drop. The revised C-9 must use a reinforced concrete stilling basin or an equivalent engineered energy dissipator.

[P64] The minimum acceptable detail is a reinforced concrete stilling basin at least 20 ft long by 36 ft wide, 12 in thick, with baffle blocks and an end sill, keyed 3 ft below grade with cutoff walls at the upstream and downstream ends and weep holes. Downstream of the basin, provide riprap with D50 = 18 in, thickness 27 in (1.5 times D50), 10 ft long by 36 ft wide, over a geotextile filter fabric, keyed into the toe. The drainage lead must demonstrate by calculation that the basin reduces the exit velocity to the riprap allowable velocity; the 18-in D50 is a minimum, not a substitute for the basin design.

[P65] 5. What the revised C-9 spillway detail must say

[P66] The revised C-9 must replace the current bullet-list detail with a dimensioned spillway plan and section. The following table is the minimum content. Each value is to be shown on the drawing and tied to the calculation sheet.

[P68] The spillway section must show the upstream and downstream water surfaces, the head H above the crest, the design WSE, the top of berm and the freeboard dimension. It must also show the existing ground at the toe (2,853.00 ft), the stilling basin, the cutoff walls, the riprap and the geotextile. A bullet list without dimensions does not satisfy G-4.

[P70] 6. What the revised C-9 basin notes must say

[P71] The current basin notes contain a correct 100-year freeboard statement (1.29 ft) but an incorrect crest offset and no spillway design basis. The notes say the crest is 0.60 ft above the 100-year water surface; the detail says 0.71 ft; the arithmetic is 0.59 ft. The revised notes must replace both numbers with 0.59 ft and must state the spillway design flow, design WSE and freeboard. The following note text is to be carried on revised C-9, with the values shown in the table above.

[P73] The revised notes must not repeat the current 0.60 ft or 0.71 ft crest offset. They must not describe the 100-year freeboard of 1.29 ft as the spillway freeboard. They must not use the 100-year, 24-hour storm as the spillway design flow; that storm governs storage volume, not peak spillway discharge.

[P74] 7. Where the overflow goes once it leaves the berm

[P75] The intended overflow path in the current record is: east berm emergency spillway → open swale in Common-Area Parcel E → Windmill Lane gutter line (C-9, Emergency Spillway Detail, p.17). From the Windmill Lane gutter line, the only receiving point of record is the shared outfall at the southwest corner of the parent parcel. The site slopes from the northeast at about 2,905 ft to the southwest outfall at about 2,850 ft (MDS Sections 2.1 and 2.4, p.3–4). The basin outlet is the existing 30-in RCP stub at the southwest corner with invert 2,850.75 ft (C-6, p.11; C-9, p.17), which connects to the CCRFCD regional facility (MDS Section 5.1, p.7; FCD acceptance letter, p.2). The overflow therefore must run west along Windmill Lane to that outfall; it cannot run east away from the only identified receiving point.

[P76] The current record does not demonstrate that path. C-9 has a note, not a plan or profile. There is no swale centerline, invert, width, slope or capacity; no gutter capacity check; and no drainage easement for the overflow across Parcel E. The final map shows a 15-ft drainage easement along the west line of Parcel D, but no overflow easement for Parcel E (Final map, Sheet 3 and Sheet 4, 08/21/2026). The overflow is also not the 30-in principal outlet; the 30-in RCP is the normal basin outlet, not an emergency spillway conduit. Sending 88.4 cfs through the 30-in outlet would be a different design and is not what C-9 shows.

[P78] Our conclusion is that the overflow is intended to end at the shared outfall and the CCRFCD regional facility, but the path is not demonstrated on the current drawings. Until the revised C-9 shows a continuous, positively graded, capacity-checked path within Parcel E and public right-of-way, G-4 cannot be closed. The final map and the drainage narrative must be consistent with that path; if an easement is needed, it must be granted by the final map under Condition 3.

[P79] 8. Does the G-4 correction trigger an amendment to the accepted Master Drainage Study?

[P80] No. The accepted MDS fixes the Phase 3 detention allocation, the 100-year water surface, the tributary breakdown and the shared outfall cap. The G-4 correction changes the spillway crest length, the top of berm and the apron detail; it does not change any of the accepted hydrologic or outfall parameters. Table 8-1 compares the accepted basis with the revised C-9.

[P81] Table 8-1 — Amendment comparison: accepted MDS basis versus revised C-9.

[P83] The MDS amendment triggers are specific. Section 4.4 says any change to the detention allocation — whether by revision of tributary area, impervious assumption, hydrologic methodology or storage-indication input — is a formal amendment. Section 7.3 says changes to the accepted detention allocations, the outfall allowance, or the tributary breakdown and phase boundaries require an amendment. The FCD acceptance letter adds any revision of phase tributary area, impervious cover, hydrologic methodology, storage-indication input, phase boundary, detention basin location, or shared outfall discharge cap. None of those changes is proposed here. The 100-year stage-storage below 2,857.91 ft, which is the storage-indication input for the accepted 100-year routing, is unchanged; the volume added by raising the top of berm is freeboard above the 100-year water surface and does not enter the accepted 100-year routing. Consistent with the June 22, 2026 pre-application notes (Section 3.2), a narrative-level reconciliation is sufficient where the Phase 3 volumes and outfall configuration match the MDS; the revised C-9 and drainage narrative will include that reconciliation.

[P84] Two record points need to be kept straight. First, the C-4 through C-7 sub-basin tabulation sums to approximately 42.05 acres, which is 2.05 acres more than the 40.0-acre Phase 3 parcel. The C-4 note explains that the excess is adjacent half-width right-of-way included for storm drain sizing. That 42.05 acres is not the detention tributary and must not be substituted for the 40.0 acres in the basin routing; doing so would be a tributary-area change and would require an amendment. Second, the preliminary detention calculation dated 09/25/2026 uses 65% impervious, 8.1 acre-feet and 6.0 cfs. It is marked PRELIMINARY — internal working file and is not adopted. If those values were used, they would change the impervious assumption, storage and release and would require an amendment. The plan and this memo use the accepted 42%, 6.4 acre-feet and 78 cfs cap.

   No formal MDS amendment is triggered by the spillway correction, provided the 100-yr WSE 2,857.91 ft, the 6.4 ac-ft Phase 3 allocation, the 40.0 ac/42% tributary basis, the Parcel E basin location, and the 78 cfs shared-outfall cap remain unchanged. The correction is a plan-level C-9 detail. Because the top of berm moves from 2,859.20 ft to 2,860.80 ft, transmit the revised C-9/spillway calculation to CCRFCD for concurrence under Condition 2; that is not a new hydrology study or amendment.
