K. Odhiambo | Clark County Development Services | Utilities coordination | In person

Callaway Land Partners was invited but did not attend; Max Braddock represented applicant-side coordination.
2. Purpose
Pre-application discussion of the Desert Sage Ranch Phase 3 improvement plan and final map resubmittal package under the current code cycle. Objective was to align the design team and County reviewers on submittal composition, review path, and any threshold issues that ought to be flagged before intake, so the package can move through Public Works plan check on the first submittal without a routing surprise.
Phase 3 is the final 40.0 acres (60 half-acre lots) of the 140-acre subdivision entitled under Tentative Map TM-22-500041 (approved 03/14/2022). Phases 1 and 2 are built and occupied; the first final map in the series was recorded in 2024.
3. Topics Discussed
3.1 Submittal package composition and application numbers. Max walked through the intended package. County has already issued application numbers on the intake pre-check:
Improvement Plans: IP-26-100288
Final Map: FM-26-100290
Package as contemplated for first submittal:
Improvement plan set (grading, drainage, streets, wet/dry utility composite) — Sundial
Landscape and irrigation set — Ocotillo Landscape Studio
Final Map (three-sheet, second in the TM-22-500041 series) — Sundial Survey
Supporting reports: updated drainage narrative referencing the approved master drainage study; geotechnical addendum; traffic memo confirming trip generation is unchanged from tentative-map assumptions
Title report and closure package — Callaway to procure through Silver Butte Title & Escrow
Agency will-serve / capacity confirmations from LVVWD and CCWRD (see 3.5)
Dale Yeoman confirmed the two application numbers above are the correct references and should appear on the title block and cover sheets of every submitted sheet. He asked that IP-26-100288 be cited on the drainage narrative title page as well.
3.2 Drainage — master study governs. Priya summarized the drainage approach: Phase 3 drains to the detention basin sized under the approved master drainage study for the subdivision. Detention allocation for Phase 3 was fixed in that study; there are no departures anticipated in the resubmittal.
Dale confirmed that so long as the Phase 3 improvement plans match the volumes and outfall configuration in the district-approved master drainage study, no fresh hydrology submittal to Regional Flood Control is required — a narrative-level reconciliation in the drainage report is sufficient. He noted plan check will still verify the basin geometry against the study.
Priya to include a reconciliation table (basin volume as built into Phase 1/2, allocations for Phase 3, and headroom) in the drainage narrative.
3.3 Landscape — significant-change threshold. Bea Cortland summarized the landscape approach: streetscape palette carried forward from the approved 2022 Phase 1/2 palette (desert planting throughout streetscapes; turf confined to the HOA common-area park). Species list is substantially the same as Phase 1/2. Some substitutions in the shrub layer may be proposed as availability has shifted since 2022.
Odette Marchetti raised that any landscape changes from the approved 2022 palette may require review beyond staff level depending on extent — the significant-change threshold has to be evaluated on the actual proposed change. She referenced condition 14 of the tentative map approval letter, which contemplates design review as a public hearing before the Town Advisory Board and Planning Commission for significant changes to approved plans, including landscape and streetscape treatments in common areas.
Discussion did not resolve where the significant-change threshold sits for this project. Odette noted the evaluation is fact-specific and that the design team should provide a red-line comparison of the proposed Phase 3 palette against the 2022 approved palette so Planning can make that call once the actual proposed change is on paper. Bea agreed to prepare that comparison as part of the landscape resubmittal.
No commitment was made at the meeting as to whether the resubmittal will or will not trigger design review. The point was flagged for the team's awareness; a written determination from Planning would follow the submittal.
3.4 Fire access. Lt. Salazar (attending for Capt. Roark) noted that the CCFD review will focus on the permanent buildout access configuration for Phase 3. The temporary secondary access accepted at Phase 2 buildout was approved as a temporary condition pending Phase 3 development, and Phase 3 improvement plans need to show the permanent second point of access consistent with the tentative map. Any deviation from what was shown on TM-22-500041 should be pre-coordinated with Capt. Roark before submittal.
Sundial to circulate the current Phase 3 access layout to CCFD in advance of the formal submittal for informal review; the substantive determination on the permanent buildout condition will come from CCFD through the plan check letter.
3.5 Utilities. K. Odhiambo confirmed that separate confirmations from Las Vegas Valley Water District (LVVWD) and Clark County Water Reclamation District (CCWRD) will be needed for the resubmittal package. These are separate agency confirmations obtained by the applicant/engineer directly with each district; the County does not procure them.
Noted for the record; no further discussion.
3.6 SWPPP / grading permit sequencing. Priya asked about sequencing between improvement plan approval and the grading permit / SWPPP. Dale confirmed the standard sequence:
Improvement plans routed and approved (IP-26-100288)
NDEP Bureau of Water Pollution Control NOI filed by contractor; SWPPP prepared under NPDES general construction permit
Grading permit application submitted to Public Works with the SWPPP and approved improvement plans referenced
Grading permit issued once bonds/estimate are posted through Callaway
The grading permit cannot issue ahead of improvement plan approval. Dale mentioned that Callaway will need to have the surety and cost estimate lined up on the Public Works side before grading permit issuance, but that this is not a first-submittal item.
4. Agreed Submittal Route
The resubmittal will be routed through Clark County Public Works, Development Review, with Comprehensive Planning coordination on the landscape and final map conditions. Dale Yeoman is the assigned civil plans examiner (Public Works). Odette Marchetti is the point of contact on the Comprehensive Planning side for the tentative map conditions carry-forward and the significant-change evaluation.
Public Works will circulate the improvement plans internally to CCFD and Landscape review. Applicant is responsible for obtaining LVVWD and CCWRD confirmations separately (see 3.5) and including them in the submittal package.
Formal intake will be at the Public Works counter under application numbers IP-26-100288 (improvement plans) and FM-26-100290 (final map).

6. Engineering Recommendations
6.1 General
The site is considered suitable for the proposed single-family residential development from a geotechnical
standpoint provided the recommendations contained herein are incorporated into project design and
construction.
6.2 Site Preparation and Earthwork
Strip and remove all surface vegetation, root mats, debris and any topsoil pockets. Anticipated stripping
depth is generally less than 6 inches across the site.
Following stripping, the exposed subgrade shall be scarified to a depth of 8 inches, moisture-conditioned to
within ±2% of optimum moisture content, and compacted to a minimum of 95% of the maximum dry density
determined by ASTM D1557.
Engineered fill shall be placed in lifts not exceeding 8 inches loose thickness, moisture-conditioned, and
compacted to a minimum of 95% of the ASTM D1557 maximum dry density.
On-site native soils, free of oversized materials (particles greater than 4 inches in maximum dimension) and
organics, are suitable for reuse as engineered fill.
Over-excavation of localized caliche crust may be required at grade transitions to establish a uniform
subgrade support condition, particularly under building pads and pavements. Where cuts expose caliche
within 12 inches of finished subgrade, we recommend over-excavation to at least 24 inches below finished
subgrade and replacement with properly compacted engineered fill.
6.3 Foundation Recommendations
Conventional continuous and isolated spread footings founded on a minimum of 24 inches of properly
compacted engineered fill, or on native soils prepared as described above, are recommended for support of the
single-family residential structures.


--- page 9 ---
• Allowable bearing pressure: 2,500 psf for dead-plus-live loads, increaseable by one-third for transient
loads (wind, seismic).
• Minimum footing width: 12 inches (continuous), 24 inches (isolated).
• Minimum embedment: 18 inches below lowest adjacent finished grade.
• Estimated total settlement: less than 1 inch; differential settlement less than ½ inch between adjacent
footings.
• Lateral resistance: coefficient of friction µ = 0.40 between footing base and compacted engineered fill;
allowable passive equivalent fluid pressure = 300 pcf against footing sides and grade beams, neglecting the
upper 12 inches.
Because the surficial soils are non-expansive (Section 4.4), post-tensioned slab-on-ground foundations are not
required from an expansion standpoint but may be selected at the structural engineer's option.

# Independent review — DSR Phase 3 emergency spillway memo (G-4)

**Deliverable reviewed:** `/filesystem/Memo_to_Callaway_Spillway_2026-10-31.docx` (14 pp., 6,990 words; format checker clean; addressed to Garrett Nokes, dated October 31, 2026, signed by Max Braddock).

**Scope of this review:** the four questions in the instruction (G-4 answerability, MDS amendment, revised C-9 content, overflow destination), the hard requirements in the 10/09/2026 CCPW G-4 letter, the accepted MDS and FCD acceptance letter, the C-9/C-6 records, the HGL/hydrology worksheets, the QA/QC checklist, the Phase 2 comments and the final map. All numbers below were recomputed independently from the source records; the author's `check_memo.py`, `requirements.csv` and tables were not used as evidence.

**Overall:** the memo is well organised and answers each question with a definite disposition, and the main weir hydraulics (20-ft and 36-ft, C = 3.0 and 2.6) are arithmetically correct. The deficiencies below are in the **conservative-case freeboard margin**, the **uncalculated stilling-basin/riprap design**, the **unresolved outlet rating that underpins the no-amendment conclusion**, and the **overflow path that relies on a gutter the County has already said is over-spread**. No BLOCKING file-format or identity error was found; the first four findings are MAJOR because they affect whether the proposed fix and the no-amendment conclusion can be relied on.

---

## 1. MAJOR — The proposed 36-ft weir passes the 1.0-ft freeboard requirement by only 0.46 in under the memo's own conservative case; it fails if the 96.8 cfs arithmetic sum is carried through 1.5Q at C = 2.6.

**Requirement.** C-9 Basin Notes (p.18): "Freeboard between the 100-year water surface (2,857.91′) and the top of berm (2,859.20′) is 1.29′, meeting the CCRFCD minimum freeboard requirement of 1.0 foot." Phase 2 comment G-3 (9/28/2022) requires "a minimum of 1.0 ft above the design HGL" and "dimensioned." The memo adopts this as "both ≥ 1.0 ft" (Table 6, "Freeboard dimension").

**What the deliverable has.** Memo §4.3 and Table 4-2 present the C = 2.6, 1.5Q case as **PASS**: H = 1.261377607 ft, WSE = 2,859.761377607 ft, freeboard = **1.038622393 ft**. That is only **0.0386 ft = 0.46 in** above the 1.0-ft limit; rounded to the 0.1-ft precision used on the drawing it is **1.0 ft**, i.e. exactly at the limit. The memo does not flag the margin and rejects a longer weir as adding "no corresponding benefit."

The memo also says in §4.1: "the spillway must pass the **unrouted** 100-year inflow without credit for the outlet," and in §4.3 checks the "arithmetic sum" **96.8 cfs** only at C = 3.0 (freeboard 1.370389398 ft). It never checks **1.5 × 96.8 = 145.2 cfs** at C = 2.6. Recomputed:

| Q (cfs) | C | L (ft) | H (ft) | WSE (ft) | Freeboard to 2,860.80 ft |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 132.6 | 2.6 | 36 | 1.261377607 | 2,859.761378 | **1.038622393** (0.46 in margin) |
| 145.2 | 2.6 | 36 | 1.340069055 | 2,859.840069 | **0.959930945 — FAILS 1.0 ft** |
| 145.2 | 3.0 | 36 | 1.218134492 | 2,859.718134 | 1.081865508 (passes) |

**What it should be.** Either (a) state plainly that 88.4 cfs is the timing-adjusted **routed** peak inflow to the basin and that 96.8 cfs is only the arithmetic sum, so the 145.2-cfs case is not the design basis; or (b) if the County/RFCD criterion is the unrouted 100-year inflow with 1.5Q, increase the weir length (a 42-ft weir at C = 2.6, 1.5Q gives 1.161812206 ft; 48 ft gives 1.258756 ft) or raise the top of berm above 2,860.80 ft. In either case, report the actual margin against 1.0 ft and do not describe the C = 2.6 / 1.5Q case as having "reserve" when it has 0.46 in.

**Evidence.** Memo §4.1 (unrouted wording), §4.3 and Table 4-2 (1.0386 PASS; 96.8 only at C = 3.0), Table 6 ("both ≥ 1.0 ft"); C-9 Basin Notes p.18; Phase 2 G-3 p.1. Recomputed values above from H = (Q/(C·L))^(2/3).

---

## 2. MAJOR — G-4 asks for sizing calculations and apron details, but the proposed stilling basin and 18-in D50 riprap are prescribed without any hydraulic sizing; the memo does not demonstrate that its own replacement apron works.

**Requirement.** CCPW 10/09/2026 G-4 (p.2): "The emergency spillway shown on Sheet C-9 lacks freeboard dimensioning and downstream apron details. Provide **sizing calculations, spillway section, and erosion protection** consistent with the RFCD Hydrologic Criteria and Drainage Design Manual." The memo itself recognises this in §4.4: "The drainage lead must demonstrate by calculation that the basin reduces the exit velocity to the riprap allowable velocity; the 18-in D50 is a minimum, not a substitute for the basin design."

**What the deliverable has.** A prescriptive "minimum acceptable detail": RC stilling basin **at least 20 ft long × 36 ft wide × 12 in thick**, baffle blocks, end sill, 3-ft cutoff walls and weep holes; downstream riprap **D50 = 18 in, 27 in thick (1.5D50), 10 ft × 36 ft**. No calculation is given for:
- inflow velocity/depth at the basin entrance (the memo gives toe velocity ≈ 19.3 ft/s but not the basin inlet Froude number);
- sequent depth and hydraulic-jump length, or the tailwater needed to hold the jump (the natural grade at the toe is 2,853.00 ft, but the basin invert and design tailwater are not stated);
- basin exit velocity versus the 18-in D50 allowable velocity (Isbash for 18-in loose rock gives about 10.86 ft/s; the memo never shows the exit velocity is below that);
- slab thickness/uplift for the 12-in basin slab;
- riprap layer thickness against D100/2D50 (27 in is 1.5D50 only).

**What it should be.** Provide the basin sizing calculation (specific energy at the toe, Froude number, sequent depth, jump length, tailwater, basin invert, exit velocity, riprap D50 and layer thickness including D100/2D50) and show the 20 × 36 × 12 basin and 18-in D50 riprap meet it. If the basin is to be sized by the drainage lead later, the memo must say the 20 × 36 × 12 and 18-in D50 are **preliminary placeholders, not a verified design**, and cannot be represented as the "minimum acceptable detail" until the calculation is done.

**Evidence.** Memo §4.4 and Table 6 ("Erosion check" says "Show calculated toe velocity ≈ 19.3 ft/s and the basin exit velocity" — no exit velocity is given); Table 7 note 5 (prescribes the basin/riprap); C-9 p.17 (existing 15 × 20 grouted riprap, D50 = 12 in); G-4 p.2. The memo's own Isbash check only sizes the **existing** 12-in stone (D50 required 4.853798953 ft = 58.25 in at 19.53 ft/s) and does not size the proposed 18-in layer.

---

## 3. MAJOR — The no-amendment conclusion rests on the 2,857.91-ft 100-year WSE, but the memo itself says the C-9 outlet detail may not reproduce the MDS outlet rating; a 12-in × 18-in orifice alone cannot pass the MDS 27.9 cfs at that WSE.

**Requirement.** FCD acceptance letter p.2: "Changes to the accepted detention allocations, outfall allowance, or the tributary area assumptions require a formal amendment ... This includes, without limitation, any proposed revision of phase tributary area, impervious cover assumption, hydrologic methodology, **storage-indication input**, phase boundary, detention basin location, or shared outfall discharge cap." MDS §4.4 (p.7) and §7.3 (p.8) to the same effect. Phase 2 comment G-2 (p.1): "The basin outlet structure detail ... does not match the sizing indicated in the drainage study. Reconcile the orifice diameter and weir crest elevation..."

All numbers below were recomputed independently from the source records; the author's `check_memo.py`, `requirements.csv` and tables were not used as evidence.

**Overall:** the memo is well organised and answers each question with a definite disposition, and the main weir hydraulics (20-ft and 36-ft, C = 3.0 and 2.6) are arithmetically correct. That is only **0.0386 ft = 0.46 in** above the 1.0-ft limit; rounded to the 0.1-ft precision used on the drawing it is **1.0 ft**, i.e. exactly at the limit. The memo does not flag the margin and rejects a longer weir as adding "no corresponding benefit."

| Q (cfs) | C | L (ft) | H (ft) | WSE (ft) | Freeboard to 2,860.80 ft |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|

# Independent review — DSR Phase 3 emergency spillway memo (G-4)

**Deliverable reviewed:** `/filesystem/Memo_to_Callaway_Spillway_2026-10-31.docx` (14 pp., 6,990 words; format checker clean; addressed to Garrett Nokes, dated October 31, 2026, signed by Max Braddock).

**Scope of this review:** the four questions in the instruction (G-4 answerability, MDS amendment, revised C-9 content, overflow destination), the hard requirements in the 10/09/2026 CCPW G-4 letter, the accepted MDS and FCD acceptance letter, the C-9/C-6 records, the HGL/hydrology worksheets, the QA/QC checklist, the Phase 2 comments and the final map. All numbers below were recomputed independently from the source records; the author's `check_memo.py`, `requirements.csv` and tables were not used as evidence.

**Overall:** the memo is well organised and answers each question with a definite disposition, and the main weir hydraulics (20-ft and 36-ft, C = 3.0 and 2.6) are arithmetically correct. The deficiencies below are in the **conservative-case freeboard margin**, the **uncalculated stilling-basin/riprap design**, the **unresolved outlet rating that underpins the no-amendment conclusion**, and the **overflow path that relies on a gutter the County has already said is over-spread**. No BLOCKING file-format or identity error was found; the first four findings are MAJOR because they affect whether the proposed fix and the no-amendment conclusion can be relied on.

---

## 1. MAJOR — The proposed 36-ft weir passes the 1.0-ft freeboard requirement by only 0.46 in under the memo's own conservative case; it fails if the 96.8 cfs arithmetic sum is carried through 1.5Q at C = 2.6.

**Requirement.** C-9 Basin Notes (p.18): "Freeboard between the 100-year water surface (2,857.91′) and the top of berm (2,859.20′) is 1.29′, meeting the CCRFCD minimum freeboard requirement of 1.0 foot." Phase 2 comment G-3 (9/28/2022) requires "a minimum of 1.0 ft above the design HGL" and "dimensioned." The memo adopts this as "both ≥ 1.0 ft" (Table 6, "Freeboard dimension").

**What the deliverable has.** Memo §4.3 and Table 4-2 present the C = 2.6, 1.5Q case as **PASS**: H = 1.261377607 ft, WSE = 2,859.761377607 ft, freeboard = **1.038622393 ft**. That is only **0.0386 ft = 0.46 in** above the 1.0-ft limit; rounded to the 0.1-ft precision used on the drawing it is **1.0 ft**, i.e. exactly at the limit. The memo does not flag the margin and rejects a longer weir as adding "no corresponding benefit."

The memo also says in §4.1: "the spillway must pass the **unrouted** 100-year inflow without credit for the outlet," and in §4.3 checks the "arithmetic sum" **96.8 cfs** only at C = 3.0 (freeboard 1.370389398 ft). It never checks **1.5 × 96.8 = 145.2 cfs** at C = 2.6. Recomputed:

| Q (cfs) | C | L (ft) | H (ft) | WSE (ft) | Freeboard to 2,860.80 ft |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 132.6 | 2.6 | 36 | 1.261377607 | 2,859.761378 | **1.038622393** (0.46 in margin) |
| 145.2 | 2.6 | 36 | 1.340069055 | 2,859.840069 | **0.959930945 — FAILS 1.0 ft** |
| 145.2 | 3.0 | 36 | 1.218134492 | 2,859.718134 | 1.081865508 (passes) |

**What it should be.** Either (a) state plainly that 88.4 cfs is the timing-adjusted **routed** peak inflow to the basin and that 96.8 cfs is only the arithmetic sum, so the 145.2-cfs case is not the design basis; or (b) if the County/RFCD criterion is the unrouted 100-year inflow with 1.5Q, increase the weir length (a 42-ft weir at C = 2.6, 1.5Q gives 1.161812206 ft; 48 ft gives 1.258756 ft) or raise the top of berm above 2,860.80 ft. In either case, report the actual margin against 1.0 ft and do not describe the C = 2.6 / 1.5Q case as having "reserve" when it has 0.46 in.

**Evidence.** Memo §4.1 (unrouted wording), §4.3 and Table 4-2 (1.0386 PASS; 96.8 only at C = 3.0), Table 6 ("both ≥ 1.0 ft"); C-9 Basin Notes p.18; Phase 2 G-3 p.1. Recomputed values above from H = (Q/(C·L))^(2/3).

---

## 2. MAJOR — G-4 asks for sizing calculations and apron details, but the proposed stilling basin and 18-in D50 riprap are prescribed without any hydraulic sizing; the memo does not demonstrate that its own replacement apron works.

**Requirement.** CCPW 10/09/2026 G-4 (p.2): "The emergency spillway shown on Sheet C-9 lacks freeboard dimensioning and downstream apron details. Provide **sizing calculations, spillway section, and erosion protection** consistent with the RFCD Hydrologic Criteria and Drainage Design Manual." The memo itself recognises this in §4.4: "The drainage lead must demonstrate by calculation that the basin reduces the exit velocity to the riprap allowable velocity; the 18-in D50 is a minimum, not a substitute for the basin design."

**What the deliverable has.** A prescriptive "minimum acceptable detail": RC stilling basin **at least 20 ft long × 36 ft wide × 12 in thick**, baffle blocks, end sill, 3-ft cutoff walls and weep holes; downstream riprap **D50 = 18 in, 27 in thick (1.5D50), 10 ft × 36 ft**. No calculation is given for:
- inflow velocity/depth at the basin entrance (the memo gives toe velocity ≈ 19.3 ft/s but not the basin inlet Froude number);
- sequent depth and hydraulic-jump length, or the tailwater needed to hold the jump (the natural grade at the toe is 2,853.00 ft, but the basin invert and design tailwater are not stated);
- basin exit velocity versus the 18-in D50 allowable velocity (Isbash for 18-in loose rock gives about 10.86 ft/s; the memo never shows the exit velocity is below that);
- slab thickness/uplift for the 12-in basin slab;
- riprap layer thickness against D100/2D50 (27 in is 1.5D50 only).

**What it should be.** Provide the basin sizing calculation (specific energy at the toe, Froude number, sequent depth, jump length, tailwater, basin invert, exit velocity, riprap D50 and layer thickness including D100/2D50) and show the 20 × 36 × 12 basin and 18-in D50 riprap meet it. If the basin is to be sized by the drainage lead later, the memo must say the 20 × 36 × 12 and 18-in D50 are **preliminary placeholders, not a verified design**, and cannot be represented as the "minimum acceptable detail" until the calculation is done.

**Evidence.** Memo §4.4 and Table 6 ("Erosion check" says "Show calculated toe velocity ≈ 19.3 ft/s and the basin exit velocity" — no exit velocity is given); Table 7 note 5 (prescribes the basin/riprap); C-9 p.17 (existing 15 × 20 grouted riprap, D50 = 12 in); G-4 p.2. The memo's own Isbash check only sizes the **existing** 12-in stone (D50 required 4.853798953 ft = 58.25 in at 19.53 ft/s) and does not size the proposed 18-in layer.

---

## 3. MAJOR — The no-amendment conclusion rests on the 2,857.91-ft 100-year WSE, but the memo itself says the C-9 outlet detail may not reproduce the MDS outlet rating; a 12-in × 18-in orifice alone cannot pass the MDS 27.9 cfs at that WSE.

**Requirement.** FCD acceptance letter p.2: "Changes to the accepted detention allocations, outfall allowance, or the tributary area assumptions require a formal amendment ... This includes, without limitation, any proposed revision of phase tributary area, impervious cover assumption, hydrologic methodology, **storage-indication input**, phase boundary, detention basin location, or shared outfall discharge cap." MDS §4.4 (p.7) and §7.3 (p.8) to the same effect. Phase 2 comment G-2 (p.1): "The basin outlet structure detail ... does not match the sizing indicated in the drainage study. Reconcile the orifice diameter and weir crest elevation..."

**What the deliverable has.** Answer 2 and Table 8-1 state that the 100-year WSE "at 2,857.91 ft ... do[es] not change," and the memo uses that WSE to fix the 0.59-ft crest offset and to conclude no MDS amendment. But Table 10 ("Outlet detail") also says: "Outlet detail may not represent the full stage-discharge rating used in the MDS; the QA/QC item 26 comparison is not a valid rating check." The C-9 outlet detail (p.18) is a **12-in high × 18-in wide orifice plate**, invert 2,851.00 ft, with a 30-in RCP downstream, and **no weir**. MDS Appendix D-2 (p.13) lists "Orifice + weir" at 2,857.00 ft and **27.9 cfs at 2,857.91 ft**. A 12 × 18 in orifice (A = 1.5 sf, Cd ≈ 0.6) at 6.91 ft head passes only about **19.0 cfs**, not 27.9 cfs; the MDS rating needs roughly 2.2 sf effective area or a weir. If the C-9 outlet is the built outlet, the actual 100-year WSE would be **higher** than 2,857.91 ft, reducing the 0.59-ft crest offset and potentially putting the spillway into operation in the 100-year event—an amendment-level change to the accepted hydrology.

**What it should be.** Before the memo states "No formal MDS amendment," reconcile the C-9 orifice/weir against the MDS Appendix D-2 stage-discharge rating and confirm the 100-year WSE remains 2,857.91 ft. Add this reconciliation to the action list with an owner and date (it is currently only in Table 10, not Table 11). If the outlet rating changes the WSE, the memo must say an amendment is required.

**Evidence.** Memo Answer 2, Table 8-1, Table 10 "Outlet detail," Table 11 (no outlet-rating action); C-9 p.18 (12 × 18 orifice, no weir); MDS Appendix D-2 p.13 (27.9 cfs at 2,857.91, "Orifice + weir" at 2,857.00); Phase 2 G-2 p.1. Recomputed orifice capacity: Q = 0.6 × 1.5 × √(2 × 32.2 × 6.91) ≈ 19.0 cfs.

---

## 4. MAJOR — The overflow destination is stated as "west along Windmill Lane," but the County's binding G-6 comment says the Windmill Lane/Desert Sage Pkwy gutter already exceeds the half-street spread criterion; the memo never cites it.

**Requirement.** CCPW 10/09/2026 G-6 (p.2), a binding General Comment: "Provide inlet capacity calculations for each on-grade and sag inlet. The gutter spread at the low point at Windmill Ln. and Desert Sage Pkwy. appears to exceed the half-street width criterion in the Uniform Standard Drawings. Revise as required." C-9 p.17: overflow "exits at Windmill Ln. gutter line."

**What the deliverable has.** Answer 4 and §7 say the overflow "must then run west along Windmill Lane to the shared outfall." The memo says the current record does not show "a gutter capacity check" and Table 8 requires a "Gutter flow profile and capacity check for 88.4 cfs; ... if the gutter is inadequate, provide a dedicated overflow channel." But it never mentions G-6, which is the County's own finding that the gutter at Windmill Ln./Desert Sage Pkwy is already over-spread. The path is therefore not merely undemonstrated—the record already indicates it is inadequate for the existing design storm, let alone 88.4 cfs of emergency overflow.

**What it should be.** State that G-6 (10/09/2026) already documents that the Windmill Lane gutter spread at the low point exceeds the half-street criterion, so the overflow cannot be assumed to run in that gutter. Commit to a dedicated overflow channel/easement (or a reconstructed gutter/inlet system) sized for 88.4 cfs, and show it on the revised C-6/C-9. This is a direct input to the answer "where the overflow ends up."

**Evidence.** CCPW 10/09/2026 G-6 p.2; Tracker Tab 1 row 6 (G-6: "gutter spread at Windmill Ln. / Desert Sage Pkwy. low point exceeds half-street criterion — revise inlet layout" — R0287); memo §7 and Table 8 (no G-6 citation); C-9 p.17.

---

## 5. MAJOR — The "No formal MDS amendment" conclusion is stated too absolutely for a change to the MDS Appendix D-2 top-of-berm (stage-storage) value; it should be conditioned on written CCRFCD concurrence under the FCD letter's "storage-indication input" trigger.

**Requirement.** FCD acceptance letter p.2: amendments include "any proposed revision of ... **storage-indication input** ..." MDS §4.4 (p.7): "Any proposed change to the detention allocation for any phase — whether by revision of tributary area, impervious assumption, hydrologic methodology or **storage-indication input** — constitutes a change to the accepted allocation and shall be processed as a formal amendment." MDS §7.3 (p.8): changes to "detention allocations, outfall allowance, or the tributary breakdown and phase boundaries" require amendment.

**What the deliverable has.** Answer 2: "**No formal amendment** to the accepted Master Drainage Study is required for the G-4 correction." Table 8-1: top of berm changes from **2,859.20 ft** (MDS Appendix D-2, p.13) to **2,860.80 ft**, marked "No formal MDS amendment; CCRFCD concurrence under Condition 2." The memo acknowledges the top of berm is an MDS Appendix D-2 value and says it will transmit for concurrence, but it still states the no-amendment conclusion in the present tense before that concurrence exists.

**What it should be.** The substance may be right—the 100-year stage-storage below 2,857.91 ft and the 6.4 ac-ft allocation are unchanged—but the memo should say: "No amendment is required **provided CCRFCD confirms** that the 2,860.80-ft top of berm is a plan-level detail and not a revision of the accepted stage-storage input; we are transmitting under Condition 2 for that written confirmation." Do not treat the question as settled until the letter is received.

**Evidence.** FCD letter p.2; MDS §4.4 p.7, §7.3 p.8, Appendix D-2 p.13 (top of berm 2,859.20); memo Answer 2, Table 8-1, §8 ("not a new hydrology study and not an amendment"). The memo's own Table 10 flags the outlet-rating uncertainty that could change the 100-year WSE (Finding 3).

## 6. MINOR — The Isbash check is applied to **grouted** riprap as if it were loose rock; the 8.865 ft/s limit and "cannot be justified by calculation" are not the applicable limits for a grouted apron.

**Requirement.** G-4 asks for erosion protection "consistent with the RFCD Hydrologic Criteria and Drainage Design Manual"; the design must use the correct erosion-protection method.

**What the deliverable has.** §4.4: "The existing apron is 15 ft by 20 ft of **grouted riprap** with D50 = 12 in ... The Isbash riprap sizing check is ... With V = 19.530989604 ft/s ... C = 0.86 ... the required D50 is 4.853798953 ft, or 58.25 in. Reversing the equation, a 12-in D50 stone is adequate only to about 8.865094247 ft/s. ... A 12-in grouted riprap apron cannot be justified by calculation."

**What it should be.** State that Isbash is a **loose-riprap** screening check and that a grouted apron's capacity is governed by the grout/foundation and the manufacturer's/standard detail's design velocity; the absence of a grouted-apron design is the real deficiency. The conclusion (provide a concrete basin) may still be correct, but the stated 8.865 ft/s limit and the "cannot be justified" wording are not supported by the method used.

**Evidence.** C-9 p.17 ("grouted rip-rap"); memo §4.4 and Table 10 ("12-in D50 adequate only to about 8.87 ft/s").

---

## 7. MINOR — The QA/QC action list omits two items that the memo's own Table 10 says must be corrected (item 26 outlet rating, item 28 section mislabel).

**Requirement.** The QA/QC checklist must be corrected and re-initialled before the revised C-9 is issued (memo §9; checklist cover "Items not initialled are open").

**What the deliverable has.** Table 10 flags QA/QC Tab 3 item 26 ("orifice diameter matches HGL worksheet ... not a valid rating check") and item 28 ("Section A-A is longitudinal; B-B is transverse — checklist mislabels the sections"). Table 11's action says only "Correct QA/QC items **27 and 29** and the Tab 3 summary, add spillway sizing check, and re-initial."

**What it should be.** Add item 26 and item 28 to the action (or state they are covered by the outlet-rating and section corrections). Otherwise the checklist can be re-initialled with the same false entries still in it.

## 8. MINOR — "Unrouted 100-year inflow" is the wrong description of the 88.4 cfs design flow; 96.8 cfs is the arithmetic sum.

**Evidence.** Memo §4.1 vs §4.2/§4.3; MDS Appendix C Table C-2 p.12; HYD Peak Flows B12–B13.

The 6.0 cfs is numerically below 78 cfs, so the "conflict with the 78 cfs cap" wording is inaccurate.

**Overall:** the memo is well organised and answers each question with a definite disposition, and the main weir hydraulics (20-ft and 36-ft, C = 3.0 and 2.6) are arithmetically correct. The deficiencies below are in the **conservative-case freeboard margin**, the **uncalculated stilling-basin/riprap design**, the **unresolved outlet rating that underpins the no-amendment conclusion**, and the **overflow path that relies on a gutter the County has already said is over-spread**. No BLOCKING file-format or identity error was found; the first five findings are MAJOR because they affect whether the proposed fix and the no-amendment conclusion can be relied on.

## 1. MAJOR — The proposed 36-ft weir passes the 1.0-ft freeboard requirement by only 0.46 in under the memo's own conservative case; it fails if the 96.8 cfs arithmetic sum is carried through 1.5Q at C = 2.6.

**Requirement.** C-9 Basin Notes (p.18): "Freeboard between the 100-year water surface (2,857.91′) and the top of berm (2,859.20′) is 1.29′, meeting the CCRFCD minimum freeboard requirement of 1.0 foot." Phase 2 comment G-3 (9/28/2022) requires "a minimum of 1.0 ft above the design HGL" and "dimensioned." The memo adopts this as "both ≥ 1.0 ft" (Table 6, "Freeboard dimension").

**What the deliverable has.** Memo §4.3 and Table 4-2 present the C = 2.6, 1.5Q case as **PASS**: H = 1.261377607 ft, WSE = 2,859.761377607 ft, freeboard = **1.038622393 ft**. That is only **0.0386 ft = 0.46 in** above the 1.0-ft limit; rounded to the 0.1-ft precision used on the drawing it is **1.0 ft**, i.e. exactly at the limit. The memo does not flag the margin and rejects a longer weir as adding "no corresponding benefit."

The memo also says in §4.1: "the spillway must pass the **unrouted** 100-year inflow without credit for the outlet," and in §4.3 checks the "arithmetic sum" **96.8 cfs** only at C = 3.0 (freeboard 1.370389398 ft). It never checks **1.5 × 96.8 = 145.2 cfs** at C = 2.6. Recomputed:

| Q (cfs) | C | L (ft) | H (ft) | WSE (ft) | Freeboard to 2,860.80 ft |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 132.6 | 2.6 | 36 | 1.261377607 | 2,859.761378 | **1.038622393** (0.46 in margin) |
| 145.2 | 2.6 | 36 | 1.340069055 | 2,859.840069 | **0.959930945 — FAILS 1.0 ft** |
| 145.2 | 3.0 | 36 | 1.218134492 | 2,859.718134 | 1.081865508 (passes) |

**What it should be.** Either (a) state plainly that 88.4 cfs is the timing-adjusted **routed** peak inflow to the basin and that 96.8 cfs is only the arithmetic sum, so the 145.2-cfs case is not the design basis; or (b) if the County/RFCD criterion is the unrouted 100-year inflow with 1.5Q, increase the weir length (a 42-ft weir at C = 2.6, 1.5Q gives 1.161812206 ft; 48 ft gives 1.258756 ft) or raise the top of berm above 2,860.80 ft. In either case, report the actual margin against 1.0 ft and do not describe the C = 2.6 / 1.5Q case as having "reserve" when it has 0.46 in.

**Evidence.** Memo §4.1 (unrouted wording), §4.3 and Table 4-2 (1.0386 PASS; 96.8 only at C = 3.0), Table 6 ("both ≥ 1.0 ft"); C-9 Basin Notes p.18; Phase 2 G-3 p.1. Recomputed values above from H = (Q/(C·L))^(2/3).

## 2. MAJOR — G-4 asks for sizing calculations and apron details, but the proposed stilling basin and 18-in D50 riprap are prescribed without any hydraulic sizing; the memo does not demonstrate that its own replacement apron works.

**Requirement.** CCPW 10/09/2026 G-4 (p.2): "The emergency spillway shown on Sheet C-9 lacks freeboard dimensioning and downstream apron details. Provide **sizing calculations, spillway section, and erosion protection** consistent with the RFCD Hydrologic Criteria and Drainage Design Manual." The memo itself recognises this in §4.4: "The drainage lead must demonstrate by calculation that the basin reduces the exit velocity to the riprap allowable velocity; the 18-in D50 is a minimum, not a substitute for the basin design."

**What the deliverable has.** A prescriptive "minimum acceptable detail": RC stilling basin **at least 20 ft long × 36 ft wide × 12 in thick**, baffle blocks, end sill, 3-ft cutoff walls and weep holes; downstream riprap **D50 = 18 in, 27 in thick (1.5D50), 10 ft × 36 ft**. No calculation is given for:
- inflow velocity/depth at the basin entrance (the memo gives toe velocity ≈ 19.3 ft/s but not the basin inlet Froude number);
- sequent depth and hydraulic-jump length, or the tailwater needed to hold the jump (the natural grade at the toe is 2,853.00 ft, but the basin invert and design tailwater are not stated);
- basin exit velocity versus the 18-in D50 allowable velocity (Isbash for 18-in loose rock gives about 10.86 ft/s; the memo never shows the exit velocity is below that);
- slab thickness/uplift for the 12-in basin slab;
- riprap layer thickness against D100/2D50 (27 in is 1.5D50 only).

**What it should be.** Provide the basin sizing calculation (specific energy at the toe, Froude number, sequent depth, jump length, tailwater, basin invert, exit velocity, riprap D50 and layer thickness including D100/2D50) and show the 20 × 36 × 12 basin and 18-in D50 riprap meet it. If the basin is to be sized by the drainage lead later, the memo must say the 20 × 36 × 12 and 18-in D50 are **preliminary placeholders, not a verified design**, and cannot be represented as the "minimum acceptable detail" until the calculation is done.

**Evidence.** Memo §4.4 and Table 6 ("Erosion check" says "Show calculated toe velocity ≈ 19.3 ft/s and the basin exit velocity" — no exit velocity is given); Table 7 note 5 (prescribes the basin/riprap); C-9 p.17 (existing 15 × 20 grouted riprap, D50 = 12 in); G-4 p.2. The memo's own Isbash check only sizes the **existing** 12-in stone (D50 required 4.853798953 ft = 58.25 in at 19.53 ft/s) and does not size the proposed 18-in layer.

## 3. MAJOR — The no-amendment conclusion rests on the 2,857.91-ft 100-year WSE, but the memo itself says the C-9 outlet detail may not reproduce the MDS outlet rating; a 12-in × 18-in orifice alone cannot pass the MDS 27.9 cfs at that WSE.

**Requirement.** FCD acceptance letter p.2: "Changes to the accepted detention allocations, outfall allowance, or the tributary area assumptions require a formal amendment ... This includes, without limitation, any proposed revision of phase tributary area, impervious cover assumption, hydrologic methodology, **storage-indication input**, phase boundary, detention basin location, or shared outfall discharge cap." MDS §4.4 (p.7) and §7.3 (p.8) to the same effect. Phase 2 comment G-2 (p.1): "The basin outlet structure detail ... does not match the sizing indicated in the drainage study. Reconcile the orifice diameter and weir crest elevation..."

**What the deliverable has.** Answer 2 and Table 8-1 state that the 100-year WSE "at 2,857.91 ft ... do[es] not change," and the memo uses that WSE to fix the 0.59-ft crest offset and to conclude no MDS amendment. But Table 10 ("Outlet detail") also says: "Outlet detail may not represent the full stage-discharge rating used in the MDS; the QA/QC item 26 comparison is not a valid rating check." The C-9 outlet detail (p.18) is a **12-in high × 18-in wide orifice plate**, invert 2,851.00 ft, with a 30-in RCP downstream, and **no weir**. MDS Appendix D-2 (p.13) lists "Orifice + weir" at 2,857.00 ft and **27.9 cfs at 2,857.91 ft**. A 12 × 18 in orifice (A = 1.5 sf, Cd ≈ 0.6) at 6.91 ft head passes only about **19.0 cfs**, not 27.9 cfs; the MDS rating needs roughly 2.2 sf effective area or a weir. If the C-9 outlet is the built outlet, the actual 100-year WSE would be **higher** than 2,857.91 ft, reducing the 0.59-ft crest offset and potentially putting the spillway into operation in the 100-year event—an amendment-level change to the accepted hydrology.

**What it should be.** Before the memo states "No formal MDS amendment," reconcile the C-9 orifice/weir against the MDS Appendix D-2 stage-discharge rating and confirm the 100-year WSE remains 2,857.91 ft. Add this reconciliation to the action list with an owner and date (it is currently only in Table 10, not Table 11). If the outlet rating changes the WSE, the memo must say an amendment is required.

**Evidence.** Memo Answer 2, Table 8-1, Table 10 "Outlet detail," Table 11 (no outlet-rating action); C-9 p.18 (12 × 18 orifice, no weir); MDS Appendix D-2 p.13 (27.9 cfs at 2,857.91, "Orifice + weir" at 2,857.00); Phase 2 G-2 p.1. Recomputed orifice capacity: Q = 0.6 × 1.5 × √(2 × 32.2 × 6.91) ≈ 19.0 cfs.

## 4. MAJOR — The overflow destination is stated as "west along Windmill Lane," but the County's binding G-6 comment says the Windmill Lane/Desert Sage Pkwy gutter already exceeds the half-street spread criterion; the memo never cites it.

**Requirement.** CCPW 10/09/2026 G-6 (p.2), a binding General Comment: "Provide inlet capacity calculations for each on-grade and sag inlet. The gutter spread at the low point at Windmill Ln. and Desert Sage Pkwy. appears to exceed the half-street width criterion in the Uniform Standard Drawings. Revise as required." C-9 p.17: overflow "exits at Windmill Ln. gutter line."

**What the deliverable has.** Answer 4 and §7 say the overflow "must then run west along Windmill Lane to the shared outfall." The memo says the current record does not show "a gutter capacity check" and Table 8 requires a "Gutter flow profile and capacity check for 88.4 cfs; ... if the gutter is inadequate, provide a dedicated overflow channel." But it never mentions G-6, which is the County's own finding that the gutter at Windmill Ln./Desert Sage Pkwy is already over-spread. The path is therefore not merely undemonstrated—the record already indicates it is inadequate for the existing design storm, let alone 88.4 cfs of emergency overflow.

**What it should be.** State that G-6 (10/09/2026) already documents that the Windmill Lane gutter spread at the low point exceeds the half-street criterion, so the overflow cannot be assumed to run in that gutter. Commit to a dedicated overflow channel/easement (or a reconstructed gutter/inlet system) sized for 88.4 cfs, and show it on the revised C-6/C-9. This is a direct input to the answer "where the overflow ends up."

**Evidence.** CCPW 10/09/2026 G-6 p.2; Tracker Tab 1 row 6 (G-6: "gutter spread at Windmill Ln. / Desert Sage Pkwy. low point exceeds half-street criterion — revise inlet layout" — R0287); memo §7 and Table 8 (no G-6 citation); C-9 p.17.

## 5. MAJOR — The "No formal MDS amendment" conclusion is stated too absolutely for a change to the MDS Appendix D-2 top-of-berm (stage-storage) value; it should be conditioned on written CCRFCD concurrence under the FCD letter's "storage-indication input" trigger.

**Requirement.** FCD acceptance letter p.2: amendments include "any proposed revision of ... **storage-indication input** ..." MDS §4.4 (p.7): "Any proposed change to the detention allocation for any phase — whether by revision of tributary area, impervious assumption, hydrologic methodology or **storage-indication input** — constitutes a change to the accepted allocation and shall be processed as a formal amendment." MDS §7.3 (p.8): changes to "detention allocations, outfall allowance, or the tributary breakdown and phase boundaries" require amendment.

**What the deliverable has.** Answer 2: "**No formal amendment** to the accepted Master Drainage Study is required for the G-4 correction." Table 8-1: top of berm changes from **2,859.20 ft** (MDS Appendix D-2, p.13) to **2,860.80 ft**, marked "No formal MDS amendment; CCRFCD concurrence under Condition 2." The memo acknowledges the top of berm is an MDS Appendix D-2 value and says it will transmit for concurrence, but it still states the no-amendment conclusion in the present tense before that concurrence exists.

**What it should be.** The substance may be right—the 100-year stage-storage below 2,857.91 ft and the 6.4 ac-ft allocation are unchanged—but the memo should say: "No amendment is required **provided CCRFCD confirms** that the 2,860.80-ft top of berm is a plan-level detail and not a revision of the accepted stage-storage input; we are transmitting under Condition 2 for that written confirmation." Do not treat the question as settled until the letter is received.

**Evidence.** FCD letter p.2; MDS §4.4 p.7, §7.3 p.8, Appendix D-2 p.13 (top of berm 2,859.20); memo Answer 2, Table 8-1, §8 ("not a new hydrology study and not an amendment"). The memo's own Table 10 flags the outlet-rating uncertainty that could change the 100-year WSE (Finding 3).

## 6. MINOR — The Isbash check is applied to **grouted** riprap as if it were loose rock; the 8.865 ft/s limit and "cannot be justified by calculation" are not the applicable limits for a grouted apron.

**Requirement.** G-4 asks for erosion protection "consistent with the RFCD Hydrologic Criteria and Drainage Design Manual"; the design must use the correct erosion-protection method.

**What the deliverable has.** §4.4: "The existing apron is 15 ft by 20 ft of **grouted riprap** with D50 = 12 in ... The Isbash riprap sizing check is ... With V = 19.530989604 ft/s ... C = 0.86 ... the required D50 is 4.853798953 ft, or 58.25 in. Reversing the equation, a 12-in D50 stone is adequate only to about 8.865094247 ft/s. ... A 12-in grouted riprap apron cannot be justified by calculation."

**What it should be.** State that Isbash is a **loose-riprap** screening check and that a grouted apron's capacity is governed by the grout/foundation and the manufacturer's/standard detail's design velocity; the absence of a grouted-apron design is the real deficiency. The conclusion (provide a concrete basin) may still be correct, but the stated 8.865 ft/s limit and the "cannot be justified" wording are not supported by the method used.

**Evidence.** C-9 p.17 ("grouted rip-rap"); memo §4.4 and Table 10 ("12-in D50 adequate only to about 8.87 ft/s").

## 8. MINOR — "Unrouted 100-year inflow" is the wrong description of the 88.4 cfs design flow; 96.8 cfs is the arithmetic sum.

**Requirement.** The design basis must be stated consistently (MDS Appendix C, Table C-2: Phase 3 "Sum of sub-basin Q100 = 96.8 cfs; Routed peak to basin = 88.4 cfs").

**What the deliverable has.** §4.1: "The emergency spillway design flow is 88.4 cfs ... the spillway must pass the **unrouted** 100-year inflow without credit for the outlet." 88.4 cfs is the **timing-adjusted/routed** peak; the unrouted arithmetic sum is 96.8 cfs (which the memo itself says in the preceding paragraph).

**What it should be.** "The 88.4 cfs timing-adjusted peak inflow to the basin" (or "100-year peak inflow"), and separately identify 96.8 cfs as the arithmetic sum. This matters because it feeds Finding 1: if the criterion is literally the unrouted 96.8 cfs, the 1.5Q/C = 2.6 case fails.

**Evidence.** Memo §4.1 vs §4.2/§4.3; MDS Appendix C Table C-2 p.12; HYD Peak Flows B12–B13.

## 9. MINOR — The preliminary detention calc's 6.0 cfs release is said to conflict with the 78 cfs cap; it does not—it is below the cap. The real conflict is the MDS's prohibition on a phase-specific outfall discharge.

**Requirement.** MDS §5.3 (p.7): "phase-level improvement plan sets are not to compute a phase-specific outfall discharge. Each phase's contribution is routed into the shared detention system, and the shared outfall discharge remains subject to the 78 cfs cap at build-out."

**What the deliverable has.** Table 10 "Preliminary detention calc": "09/25/2026: 65% impervious, 8.1 acre-feet, 6.0 cfs release, 66.5-acre composite | Conflicts with accepted MDS 42%, 6.4 acre-feet, **78 cfs cap**; not adopted."

**What it should be.** "The 6.0 cfs phase-specific release conflicts with MDS §5.3, which prohibits a phase-specific outfall discharge; the 65% impervious and 8.1 ac-ft conflict with the accepted 42% and 6.4 ac-ft allocation." The 6.0 cfs is numerically below 78 cfs, so the "conflict with the 78 cfs cap" wording is inaccurate.

**Evidence.** Prelim calc Detention Sizing B15 (6.0 cfs); MDS §5.3 p.7; MDS Table 4-1 p.6; memo Table 10.

exit_code=0
# Independent review — DSR Phase 3 emergency spillway memo (G-4)

**Deliverable reviewed:** `/filesystem/Memo_to_Callaway_Spillway_2026-10-31.docx` (14 pp., 6,990 words; format checker clean; addressed to Garrett Nokes, dated October 31, 2026, signed by Max Braddock).

**Scope of this review:** the four questions in the instruction (G-4 answerability, MDS amendment, revised C-9 content, overflow destination), the hard requirements in the 10/09/2026 CCPW G-4 letter, the accepted MDS and FCD acceptance letter, the C-9/C-6 records, the HGL/hydrology worksheets, the QA/QC checklist, the Phase 2 comments and the final map. All numbers below were recomputed independently from the source records; the author's `check_memo.py`, `requirements.csv` and tables were not used as evidence.

**Overall:** the memo is well organised and answers each question with a definite disposition, and the main weir hydraulics (20-ft and 36-ft, C = 3.0 and 2.6) are arithmetically correct. The deficiencies below are in the **conservative-case freeboard margin**, the **uncalculated stilling-basin/riprap design**, the **unresolved outlet rating that underpins the no-amendment conclusion**, and the **overflow path that relies on a gutter the County has already said is over-spread**. No BLOCKING file-format or identity error was found; the first five findings are MAJOR because they affect whether the proposed fix and the no-amendment conclusion can be relied on.

---

## 1. MAJOR — The proposed 36-ft weir passes the 1.0-ft freeboard requirement by only 0.46 in under the memo's own conservative case; it fails if the 96.8 cfs arithmetic sum is carried through 1.5Q at C = 2.6.

**Requirement.** C-9 Basin Notes (p.18): "Freeboard between the 100-year water surface (2,857.91′) and the top of berm (2,859.20′) is 1.29′, meeting the CCRFCD minimum freeboard requirement of 1.0 foot." Phase 2 comment G-3 (9/28/2022) requires "a minimum of 1.0 ft above the design HGL" and "dimensioned." The memo adopts this as "both ≥ 1.0 ft" (Table 6, "Freeboard dimension").

**What the deliverable has.** Memo §4.3 and Table 4-2 present the C = 2.6, 1.5Q case as **PASS**: H = 1.261377607 ft, WSE = 2,859.761377607 ft, freeboard = **1.038622393 ft**. That is only **0.0386 ft = 0.46 in** above the 1.0-ft limit; rounded to the 0.1-ft precision used on the drawing it is **1.0 ft**, i.e. exactly at the limit. The memo does not flag the margin and rejects a longer weir as adding "no corresponding benefit."

The memo also says in §4.1: "the spillway must pass the **unrouted** 100-year inflow without credit for the outlet," and in §4.3 checks the "arithmetic sum" **96.8 cfs** only at C = 3.0 (freeboard 1.370389398 ft). It never checks **1.5 × 96.8 = 145.2 cfs** at C = 2.6. Recomputed:

| Q (cfs) | C | L (ft) | H (ft) | WSE (ft) | Freeboard to 2,860.80 ft |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 132.6 | 2.6 | 36 | 1.261377607 | 2,859.761378 | **1.038622393** (0.46 in margin) |
| 145.2 | 2.6 | 36 | 1.340069055 | 2,859.840069 | **0.959930945 — FAILS 1.0 ft** |
| 145.2 | 3.0 | 36 | 1.218134492 | 2,859.718134 | 1.081865508 (passes) |

**What it should be.** Either (a) state plainly that 88.4 cfs is the timing-adjusted **routed** peak inflow to the basin and that 96.8 cfs is only the arithmetic sum, so the 145.2-cfs case is not the design basis; or (b) if the County/RFCD criterion is the unrouted 100-year inflow with 1.5Q, increase the weir length (a 42-ft weir at C = 2.6, 1.5Q gives 1.161812206 ft; 48 ft gives 1.258756 ft) or raise the top of berm above 2,860.80 ft. In either case, report the actual margin against 1.0 ft and do not describe the C = 2.6 / 1.5Q case as having "reserve" when it has 0.46 in.

**Evidence.** Memo §4.1 (unrouted wording), §4.3 and Table 4-2 (1.0386 PASS; 96.8 only at C = 3.0), Table 6 ("both ≥ 1.0 ft"); C-9 Basin Notes p.18; Phase 2 G-3 p.1. Recomputed values above from H = (Q/(C·L))^(2/3).

---

## 2. MAJOR — G-4 asks for sizing calculations and apron details, but the proposed stilling basin and 18-in D50 riprap are prescribed without any hydraulic sizing; the memo does not demonstrate that its own replacement apron works.

**Requirement.** CCPW 10/09/2026 G-4 (p.2): "The emergency spillway shown on Sheet C-9 lacks freeboard dimensioning and downstream apron details. Provide **sizing calculations, spillway section, and erosion protection** consistent with the RFCD Hydrologic Criteria and Drainage Design Manual." The memo itself recognises this in §4.4: "The drainage lead must demonstrate by calculation that the basin reduces the exit velocity to the riprap allowable velocity; the 18-in D50 is a minimum, not a substitute for the basin design."

**What the deliverable has.** A prescriptive "minimum acceptable detail": RC stilling basin **at least 20 ft long × 36 ft wide × 12 in thick**, baffle blocks, end sill, 3-ft cutoff walls and weep holes; downstream riprap **D50 = 18 in, 27 in thick (1.5D50), 10 ft × 36 ft**. No calculation is given for:
- inflow velocity/depth at the basin entrance (the memo gives toe velocity ≈ 19.3 ft/s but not the basin inlet Froude number);
- sequent depth and hydraulic-jump length, or the tailwater needed to hold the jump (the natural grade at the toe is 2,853.00 ft, but the basin invert and design tailwater are not stated);
- basin exit velocity versus the 18-in D50 allowable velocity (Isbash for 18-in loose rock gives about 10.86 ft/s; the memo never shows the exit velocity is below that);
- slab thickness/uplift for the 12-in basin slab;
- riprap layer thickness against D100/2D50 (27 in is 1.5D50 only).

**What it should be.** Provide the basin sizing calculation (specific energy at the toe, Froude number, sequent depth, jump length, tailwater, basin invert, exit velocity, riprap D50 and layer thickness including D100/2D50) and show the 20 × 36 × 12 basin and 18-in D50 riprap meet it. If the basin is to be sized by the drainage lead later, the memo must say the 20 × 36 × 12 and 18-in D50 are **preliminary placeholders, not a verified design**, and cannot be represented as the "minimum acceptable detail" until the calculation is done.

**Evidence.** Memo §4.4 and Table 6 ("Erosion check" says "Show calculated toe velocity ≈ 19.3 ft/s and the basin exit velocity" — no exit velocity is given); Table 7 note 5 (prescribes the basin/riprap); C-9 p.17 (existing 15 × 20 grouted riprap, D50 = 12 in); G-4 p.2. The memo's own Isbash check only sizes the **existing** 12-in stone (D50 required 4.853798953 ft = 58.25 in at 19.53 ft/s) and does not size the proposed 18-in layer.

---

## 3. MAJOR — The no-amendment conclusion rests on the 2,857.91-ft 100-year WSE, but the memo itself says the C-9 outlet detail may not reproduce the MDS outlet rating; a 12-in × 18-in orifice alone cannot pass the MDS 27.9 cfs at that WSE.

**Requirement.** FCD acceptance letter p.2: "Changes to the accepted detention allocations, outfall allowance, or the tributary area assumptions require a formal amendment ... This includes, without limitation, any proposed revision of phase tributary area, impervious cover assumption, hydrologic methodology, **storage-indication input**, phase boundary, detention basin location, or shared outfall discharge cap." MDS §4.4 (p.7) and §7.3 (p.8) to the same effect. Phase 2 comment G-2 (p.1): "The basin outlet structure detail ... does not match the sizing indicated in the drainage study. Reconcile the orifice diameter and weir crest elevation..."

**What the deliverable has.** Answer 2 and Table 8-1 state that the 100-year WSE "at 2,857.91 ft ... do[es] not change," and the memo uses that WSE to fix the 0.59-ft crest offset and to conclude no MDS amendment. But Table 10 ("Outlet detail") also says: "Outlet detail may not represent the full stage-discharge rating used in the MDS; the QA/QC item 26 comparison is not a valid rating check." The C-9 outlet detail (p.18) is a **12-in high × 18-in wide orifice plate**, invert 2,851.00 ft, with a 30-in RCP downstream, and **no weir**. MDS Appendix D-2 (p.13) lists "Orifice + weir" at 2,857.00 ft and **27.9 cfs at 2,857.91 ft**. A 12 × 18 in orifice (A = 1.5 sf, Cd ≈ 0.6) at 6.91 ft head passes only about **19.0 cfs**, not 27.9 cfs; the MDS rating needs roughly 2.2 sf effective area or a weir. If the C-9 outlet is the built outlet, the actual 100-year WSE would be **higher** than 2,857.91 ft, reducing the 0.59-ft crest offset and potentially putting the spillway into operation in the 100-year event—an amendment-level change to the accepted hydrology.

**What it should be.** Before the memo states "No formal MDS amendment," reconcile the C-9 orifice/weir against the MDS Appendix D-2 stage-discharge rating and confirm the 100-year WSE remains 2,857.91 ft. Add this reconciliation to the action list with an owner and date (it is currently only in Table 10, not Table 11). If the outlet rating changes the WSE, the memo must say an amendment is required.

**Evidence.** Memo Answer 2, Table 8-1, Table 10 "Outlet detail," Table 11 (no outlet-rating action); C-9 p.18 (12 × 18 orifice, no weir); MDS Appendix D-2 p.13 (27.9 cfs at 2,857.91, "Orifice + weir" at 2,857.00); Phase 2 G-2 p.1. Recomputed orifice capacity: Q = 0.6 × 1.5 × √(2 × 32.2 × 6.91) ≈ 19.0 cfs.

---

## 4. MAJOR — The overflow destination is stated as "west along Windmill Lane," but the County's binding G-6 comment says the Windmill Lane/Desert Sage Pkwy gutter already exceeds the half-street spread criterion; the memo never cites it.

**Requirement.** CCPW 10/09/2026 G-6 (p.2), a binding General Comment: "Provide inlet capacity calculations for each on-grade and sag inlet. The gutter spread at the low point at Windmill Ln. and Desert Sage Pkwy. appears to exceed the half-street width criterion in the Uniform Standard Drawings. Revise as required." C-9 p.17: overflow "exits at Windmill Ln. gutter line."

**What the deliverable has.** Answer 4 and §7 say the overflow "must then run west along Windmill Lane to the shared outfall." The memo says the current record does not show "a gutter capacity check" and Table 8 requires a "Gutter flow profile and capacity check for 88.4 cfs; ... if the gutter is inadequate, provide a dedicated overflow channel." But it never mentions G-6, which is the County's own finding that the gutter at Windmill Ln./Desert Sage Pkwy is already over-spread. The path is therefore not merely undemonstrated—the record already indicates it is inadequate for the existing design storm, let alone 88.4 cfs of emergency overflow.

**What it should be.** State that G-6 (10/09/2026) already documents that the Windmill Lane gutter spread at the low point exceeds the half-street criterion, so the overflow cannot be assumed to run in that gutter. Commit to a dedicated overflow channel/easement (or a reconstructed gutter/inlet system) sized for 88.4 cfs, and show it on the revised C-6/C-9. This is a direct input to the answer "where the overflow ends up."

**Evidence.** CCPW 10/09/2026 G-6 p.2; Tracker Tab 1 row 6 (G-6: "gutter spread at Windmill Ln. / Desert Sage Pkwy. low point exceeds half-street criterion — revise inlet layout" — R0287); memo §7 and Table 8 (no G-6 citation); C-9 p.17.

---

## 5. MAJOR — The "No formal MDS amendment" conclusion is stated too absolutely for a change to the MDS Appendix D-2 top-of-berm (stage-storage) value; it should be conditioned on written CCRFCD concurrence under the FCD letter's "storage-indication input" trigger.

**Requirement.** FCD acceptance letter p.2: amendments include "any proposed revision of ... **storage-indication input** ..." MDS §4.4 (p.7): "Any proposed change to the detention allocation for any phase — whether by revision of tributary area, impervious assumption, hydrologic methodology or **storage-indication input** — constitutes a change to the accepted allocation and shall be processed as a formal amendment." MDS §7.3 (p.8): changes to "detention allocations, outfall allowance, or the tributary breakdown and phase boundaries" require amendment.

**What the deliverable has.** Answer 2: "**No formal amendment** to the accepted Master Drainage Study is required for the G-4 correction." Table 8-1: top of berm changes from **2,859.20 ft** (MDS Appendix D-2, p.13) to **2,860.80 ft**, marked "No formal MDS amendment; CCRFCD concurrence under Condition 2." The memo acknowledges the top of berm is an MDS Appendix D-2 value and says it will transmit for concurrence, but it still states the no-amendment conclusion in the present tense before that concurrence exists.

**What it should be.** The substance may be right—the 100-year stage-storage below 2,857.91 ft and the 6.4 ac-ft allocation are unchanged—but the memo should say: "No amendment is required **provided CCRFCD confirms** that the 2,860.80-ft top of berm is a plan-level detail and not a revision of the accepted stage-storage input; we are transmitting under Condition 2 for that written confirmation." Do not treat the question as settled until the letter is received.

**Evidence.** FCD letter p.2; MDS §4.4 p.7, §7.3 p.8, Appendix D-2 p.13 (top of berm 2,859.20); memo Answer 2, Table 8-1, §8 ("not a new hydrology study and not an amendment"). The memo's own Table 10 flags the outlet-rating uncertainty that could change the 100-year WSE (Finding 3).

---

## 6. MINOR — The Isbash check is applied to **grouted** riprap as if it were loose rock; the 8.865 ft/s limit and "cannot be justified by calculation" are not the applicable limits for a grouted apron.

**Requirement.** G-4 asks for erosion protection "consistent with the RFCD Hydrologic Criteria and Drainage Design Manual"; the design must use the correct erosion-protection method.

**What the deliverable has.** §4.4: "The existing apron is 15 ft by 20 ft of **grouted riprap** with D50 = 12 in ... The Isbash riprap sizing check is ... With V = 19.530989604 ft/s ... C = 0.86 ... the required D50 is 4.853798953 ft, or 58.25 in. Reversing the equation, a 12-in D50 stone is adequate only to about 8.865094247 ft/s. ... A 12-in grouted riprap apron cannot be justified by calculation."

**What it should be.** State that Isbash is a **loose-riprap** screening check and that a grouted apron's capacity is governed by the grout/foundation and the manufacturer's/standard detail's design velocity; the absence of a grouted-apron design is the real deficiency. The conclusion (provide a concrete basin) may still be correct, but the stated 8.865 ft/s limit and the "cannot be justified" wording are not supported by the method used.

**Evidence.** C-9 p.17 ("grouted rip-rap"); memo §4.4 and Table 10 ("12-in D50 adequate only to about 8.87 ft/s").

---

## 7. MINOR — The QA/QC action list omits two items that the memo's own Table 10 says must be corrected (item 26 outlet rating, item 28 section mislabel).

**Requirement.** The QA/QC checklist must be corrected and re-initialled before the revised C-9 is issued (memo §9; checklist cover "Items not initialled are open").

**What the deliverable has.** Table 10 flags QA/QC Tab 3 item 26 ("orifice diameter matches HGL worksheet ... not a valid rating check") and item 28 ("Section A-A is longitudinal; B-B is transverse — checklist mislabels the sections"). #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Independent check of the G-4 spillway memo against its requirements table and key calculations."""
import csv, math, os, re, sys
from docx import Document

MEMO = "/filesystem/Memo_to_Callaway_Spillway_2026-10-31.docx"
REQ = "/tmp/ahpele/requirements.csv"
TOL = 1e-9
fails = []
checks = 0

def ok(cond, msg):
    global checks
    checks += 1
    if not cond:
        fails.append(msg)

def num_tokens(s):
    s = s.replace("\u2212", "-").replace("–", "-").replace("—", "-")
    return re.findall(r"[-+]?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?", s)

def norm_num(x):
    x = x.replace(",", "")
    try:
        return float(x)
    except ValueError:
        return None

def read_memo(path):
    doc = Document(path)
    parts = [p.text for p in doc.paragraphs]
    for t in doc.tables:
        for row in t.rows:
            for cell in row.cells:
                parts.append(cell.text)
    return doc, "\n".join(parts)

# 1. File and DOCX schema
ok(os.path.isfile(MEMO), "Memo file missing")
doc, text = read_memo(MEMO)
ok(len(text.split()) > 1500, "Memo too short")
for bad in ["TBD", "TBA", "TODO", "FIXME", "lorem ipsum", "XXX"]:
    ok(bad.lower() not in text.lower(), f"Placeholder text found: {bad}")
for required in ["October 31, 2026", "Garrett Nokes", "Callaway Land Partners", "G-4",
                 "No formal amendment", "36-ft", "2,860.80", "88.4", "1.294793994",
                 "0.594793994", "1.424977931", "1.153396722", "D50 = 18 in",
                 "Windmill", "shared outfall", "0.59 ft", "6.4 acre-feet", "66.5"]:
    ok(required in text, f"Required memo content missing: {required}")
ok(len(doc.tables) >= 8, "Expected at least 8 tables")
for ti, t in enumerate(doc.tables, 1):
    for ri, row in enumerate(t.rows):
        for ci, cell in enumerate(row.cells):
            ok(cell.text.strip() != "", f"Empty table cell: table {ti}, row {ri+1}, col {ci+1}")

# 2. Recomputed hydraulics
Q100 = 88.4
Q15 = 1.5 * Q100
C = 3.0
Lold = 20.0
Lnew = 36.0
crest = 2858.50
wse100 = 2857.91
top_old = 2859.20
top_new = 2860.80
H_old = (Q100 / (C * Lold)) ** (2/3)
wse_old = crest + H_old
over_old = wse_old - top_old
cap_old = C * Lold * (top_old - crest) ** 1.5
L_req = Q100 / (C * (top_old - crest) ** 1.5)
H_credit = ((Q100 - 41.5) / (C * Lold)) ** (2/3)
wse_credit = crest + H_credit
over_credit = wse_credit - top_old
H_new = (Q100 / (C * Lnew)) ** (2/3)
wse_new = crest + H_new
fb_new = top_new - wse_new
H_new15 = (Q15 / (C * Lnew)) ** (2/3)
wse_new15 = crest + H_new15
fb_new15 = top_new - wse_new15
H_new26 = (Q100 / (2.6 * Lnew)) ** (2/3)
wse_new26 = crest + H_new26
fb_new26 = top_new - wse_new26
H_new1526 = (Q15 / (2.6 * Lnew)) ** (2/3)
wse_new1526 = crest + H_new1526
fb_new1526 = top_new - wse_new1526
# toe velocity, existing 20 ft weir
qold = Q100 / Lold
dc_old = (qold * qold / 32.2) ** (1/3)
vc_old = qold / dc_old
vtoe_old = math.sqrt(vc_old * vc_old + 2 * 32.2 * (crest - 2853.00))
D50_toe = vtoe_old ** 2 / (2 * 32.2 * 0.86 ** 2 * (2.65 - 1))
v_allow_12 = math.sqrt(2 * 32.2 * 0.86 ** 2 * (2.65 - 1) * 1.0)

expected = {
    "crest offset 2,858.50-2,857.91": (crest - wse100, 0.59),
    "existing head": (H_old, 1.294793994),
    "existing WSE": (wse_old, 2859.794793994),
    "existing overtopping": (over_old, 0.594793994),
    "existing capacity at 0.70 ft": (cap_old, 35.139721114),
    "required crest length at 0.70 ft": (L_req, 50.313432888),
    "credited-outlet head": (H_credit, 0.848557080),
    "credited-outlet overtopping": (over_credit, 0.148557080),
    "proposed head Q100": (H_new, 0.875022069),
    "proposed WSE Q100": (wse_new, 2859.375022069),
    "proposed freeboard Q100": (fb_new, 1.424977931),
    "proposed head 1.5Q": (H_new15, 1.146603278),
    "proposed freeboard 1.5Q": (fb_new15, 1.153396722),
    "C=2.6 Q100 head": (H_new26, 0.962611275),
    "C=2.6 Q100 freeboard": (fb_new26, 1.337388725),
    "C=2.6 1.5Q head": (H_new1526, 1.261377607),
    "C=2.6 1.5Q freeboard": (fb_new1526, 1.038622393),
    "toe velocity existing weir": (vtoe_old, 19.530989604),
    "Isbash D50 existing weir": (D50_toe, 4.853798953),
    "12-in D50 allowable velocity": (v_allow_12, 8.865094247),
}
for name, (calc, shown) in expected.items():
    ok(abs(calc - shown) < 1e-6, f"{name}: calc {calc:.9f}, memo/check {shown:.9f}")
# The memo text must contain the full-precision values it claims
for s in ["1.294793994", "2,859.794793994", "0.594793994", "35.139721114",
          "50.313432888", "0.848557080", "0.148557080", "0.875022069",
          "2,859.375022069", "1.424977931", "1.146603278", "1.153396722",
          "0.962611275", "1.337388725", "1.261377607", "1.038622393",
          "19.530989604", "4.853798953", "8.865094247"]:
    ok(s in text, f"Full-precision value missing from memo: {s}")

# 3. C-9 storage table recomputation
elev = [2851.00, 2852.00, 2853.00, 2854.00, 2855.00, 2856.00, 2857.00, 2857.91, 2858.50, 2859.20]
area = [29450, 32380, 35420, 38600, 41910, 45340, 48900, 52250, 54480, 57180]
cum = [0.0]
for i in range(1, len(elev)):
    inc = (area[i-1] + area[i]) / 2.0 * (elev[i] - elev[i-1]) / 43560.0
    cum.append(cum[-1] + inc)
ok(abs(cum[7] - 6.40) < 0.005, f"C-9 100-yr storage recomputes {cum[7]:.4f}, not 6.40")
ok(abs(cum[8] - 7.12) < 0.005, f"C-9 crest storage recomputes {cum[8]:.4f}, not 7.12")
ok(abs(cum[9] - 8.02) < 0.005, f"C-9 top-of-berm storage recomputes {cum[9]:.4f}, not 8.02")
for s in ["6.40", "7.12", "8.02", "2.89"]:
    ok(s in text, f"Storage/freeboard value missing from memo: {s}")

# 4. Requirements table coverage
with open(REQ, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    reqs = list(csv.DictReader(fh))
ok(len(reqs) >= 40, f"Requirements table has only {len(reqs)} rows")
memo_nums = set()
for tok in num_tokens(text):
    v = norm_num(tok)
    if v is not None:
        memo_nums.add(round(v, 6))
no_value_keywords = {
    "R-08": "G-4", "R-11": "amendment", "R-12": "deviation", "R-25": "maintained",
    "R-26": "basin summary", "R-32": "drainage study", "R-33": "fresh hydrology",
    "R-36": "open swale", "R-38": "basin location", "R-39": "QA/QC", "R-40": "Parcel E",
    "R-41": "outlet detail", "R-42": "drainage easement", "R-43": "revision",
    "R-46": "detention allocation", "R-47": "outfall allowance",
}
for r in reqs:
    rid = r["req_id"]
    sv = r["source_value"].strip()
    if sv:
        missing = []
        for tok in num_tokens(sv):
            v = norm_num(tok)
            if v is None:
                continue
            if round(v, 6) not in memo_nums:
                missing.append(tok)
        ok(not missing, f"{rid}: source value(s) not found in memo: {missing}")
    else:
        kw = no_value_keywords.get(rid)
        if kw:
            ok(kw.lower() in text.lower(), f"{rid}: keyword '{kw}' not found in memo")

# 5. Date, addressee, signature
ok("October 31, 2026" in text and "Date: October 31, 2026" in text, "Date missing or wrong")
ok("Max Braddock" in text and "Project Manager" in text, "Signature block missing")
ok("Garrett Nokes" in text and "Callaway Land Partners" in text, "Addressee missing")

# Worst-case utilisation summary
print("Worst-case utilisation of the governing limits:")
print(f"  Existing 20-ft weir head / available head: {H_old/0.70:.3f} (design H {H_old:.6f} ft vs 0.70 ft available)")
print(f"  Existing 20-ft weir capacity / design Q: {Q100/cap_old:.3f} (design Q {Q100:.1f} cfs vs {cap_old:.3f} cfs capacity)")
print(f"  Proposed 36-ft weir freeboard requirement / provided, Q100: {1.0/fb_new:.3f} (1.0 ft required vs {fb_new:.6f} ft provided)")
print(f"  Proposed 36-ft weir freeboard requirement / provided, 1.5Q: {1.0/fb_new15:.3f} (1.0 ft required vs {fb_new15:.6f} ft provided)")
print(f"  Existing 12-in D50 riprap / required D50: {1.0/D50_toe:.3f} (12 in provided vs {D50_toe*12:.3f} in required by Isbash)")
print(f"  Existing toe velocity / 12-in D50 allowable velocity: {vtoe_old/v_allow_12:.3f} ({vtoe_old:.3f} ft/s vs {v_allow_12:.3f} ft/s)")

if fails:
    print(f"FAIL: {len(fails)} problem(s) in {checks} checks")
    for f in fails:

print(f"PASS: {checks} checks; all key calculations, requirement values, date/addressee and DOCX schema rules verified.")

   No. C-9 has no spillway sizing calculation, no spillway section/freeboard dimension from the spillway design WSE, and no apron/erosion design. The 20-ft x 6-ft broad-crested weir is undersized: at the 100-yr Phase 3 inflow of 88.4 cfs with the outlet blocked, required head is 1.2948 ft but only 0.70 ft is available to top of berm; it overtops the berm by 0.5948 ft. See memo §3 and §4.

2. **Does the G-4 revision trigger an amendment to the accepted master drainage study?**
   No formal MDS amendment is triggered by the spillway correction, provided the 100-yr WSE 2,857.91 ft, the 6.4 ac-ft Phase 3 allocation, the 40.0 ac/42% tributary basis, the Parcel E basin location, and the 78 cfs shared-outfall cap remain unchanged. The correction is a plan-level C-6/C-9 detail. Because the top of berm moves from 2,859.20 ft to 2,860.80 ft, transmit the revised C-9/spillway calculation to CCRFCD for concurrence under Condition 2; that is not a new hydrology study or amendment. See memo §7.

3. **What must the spillway detail and basin notes say on the revised C-9?**
   Spillway crest 2,858.50 ft (0.59 ft above 100-yr WSE 2,857.91 ft, not 0.60 or 0.71); design flow 88.4 cfs with outlet blocked; 1.5Q check 132.6 cfs; minimum 36-ft broad-crested weir, C = 3.0, head 0.875 ft at Q100; top of berm 2,860.80 ft; freeboard 1.425 ft at Q100 and 1.153 ft at 1.5Q (C = 2.6 also passes); 12-in x 18-in ACB crest, cutoff walls; reinforced concrete stilling basin at least 20 ft x 36 ft x 12 in with baffle blocks/end sill and 3-ft cutoff; downstream riprap D50 18 in, 27 in thick, 10 ft. Basin notes must state the design flow, spillway design WSE and freeboard, the 6.4 ac-ft allocation/provided volume, and the MDS reference. The RFCD manual text itself is not in the record set; the memo applies the conservative 100-year blocked-outlet check and a 1.5Q check and confirms both. See memo §4, §5 and §6.

4. **Where does the overflow end up once it leaves the berm?**
   East berm spillway -> open swale in Common-Area Parcel E -> Windmill Lane gutter line -> west along Windmill Lane to the shared outfall at the southwest corner -> CCRFCD regional facility. The current C-9 does not show a continuous swale alignment/inverts, capacity check or drainage easement; the revised C-9 must show the path wholly within Parcel E/public ROW or add a drainage easement. The overflow is not routed through the 30-in principal outlet pipe. See memo §6.

5. **Work against the improvement plans and QA/QC checklist.**
   Done. C-1, C-6 and C-9 values checked; QA/QC Tab 3 is wrong to certify Detail 4 as complete and mislabels Section A-A as typical and Section B-B as the outlet swale (A-A is longitudinal through the outlet; B-B is transverse). See memo §2 and §8.

6. **Work against the master drainage study and storm drain worksheets.**
   Done. MDS Rev 1 Feb 2022 Table 4-1, Appendix C, Appendix D-2; Storm Drain HGL July 2026 Inputs/HGL Summary. Spillway design flow 88.4 cfs and 100-yr WSE 2,857.91 ft confirmed. See memo §2 and §3.

7. **Work against the Phase 2 comments and FCD acceptance letter.**
   Done. Phase 2 G-3 freeboard 1.0 ft requirement and G-2 outlet-detail reconciliation are carried; FCD 2/28/2022 amendment triggers are applied. See memo §2 and §7. CCRFCD concurrence is the schedule-critical item; memo §10 sets 11/18/2026 transmittal and a 11/25/2026 fallback so the 11/30/2026 resubmittal is not held.

8. **Memo to Callaway for signature, dated 10/31/2026.**
   Delivered at `/filesystem/Memo_to_Callaway_Spillway_2026-10-31.docx`, addressed to Garrett Nokes, Callaway Land Partners, with signature block for Max Braddock, PM.

9. **Commit to one disposition on each question.**
   Memo gives one disposition per question; no alternatives presented as choices.

10. **Units on every value and name the record.**
    Every value in the memo carries units and a record citation (document, section/table/page/date). See memo tables and footnotes.

11. **Do not round intermediate values.**
    Calculations show full precision intermediate values; final values rounded only for presentation.

12. **Professional engineering standards.**
    Memo applies CCRFCD detention/spillway practice, broad-crested weir hydraulics, Isbash riprap check, geotechnical subgrade preparation and engineered-fill compaction (8-in scarify/lifts, 95% ASTM D1557) for the 1.60-ft berm raise, and clearly separates the accepted design basis from preliminary/non-adopted records. See memo §4.3 and §10.
